options.text: Create documents with the relevant information. Store the documents in Amazon S3.
Use AWS AI Service Cards for transparency and understanding models.
Create Amazon SageMaker Model Cards with intended uses and training and inference details.
Create model training scripts. Commit the model training scripts to a Git repository.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Cards provide a standardized, structured format to document model details including intended use cases, training methodology, performance metrics, evaluation results, ethical considerations, and version history. This facilitates comprehensive auditing, transparency, and accountability when sharing models across teams. Other options lack the standardization and audit-specific features needed for model governance.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker Model Cards](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-cards.html)

A company has deployed an AI application to production on AWS, and the application's responses have grown less accurate over time.  
  
The company requires a solution that sends alerts when application performance drifts.  
  
Which AWS service or feature meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors ML models in production, including model-quality metrics such as accuracy. It detects deviations from configured baselines or thresholds and supports alerts when model performance drifts.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Model quality metrics and Amazon CloudWatch monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-model-quality-metrics.html)

questions.question:
A company uses Amazon SageMaker to deploy a model that determines whether social media posts contain specific topics. The company must demonstrate how different input features affect the model's behavior.  
  
Which SageMaker feature satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify provides model explainability through feature attribution, showing how individual input features contribute to model predictions. It also supports NLP explainability for text features.\
\
**Learn more:** [Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-explainability.html) · [ClarifyTextConfig - Amazon SageMaker API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClarifyTextConfig.html)

questions.question: Which option describes a characteristic of transformer-based language models?

options.text: Transformer-based language models use convolutional layers to apply filters across an input to capture local patterns through filtered views.
Transformer-based language models can process only text data.
Transformer-based language models use self-attention mechanisms to capture contextual relationships.
Transformer-based language models process data sequences one element at a time in cyclic iterations.

questions.explanation:
Transformer-based language models use self-attention to model contextual relationships among tokens in an input sequence. This enables each token representation to incorporate relevant information from other tokens.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Transformers? (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/transformers-in-artificial-intelligence/)

An AI practitioner trained a custom model on Amazon Bedrock by using a training dataset that contains confidential data. The AI practitioner wants to ensure that the custom model does not generate inference responses based on confidential data.  

How should the AI practitioner prevent responses based on confidential data?

options.text: Delete the custom model. Remove the confidential data from the training dataset. Retrain the custom model.
Mask the confidential data in the inference responses by using dynamic data masking.
Encrypt the confidential data in the inference responses by using Amazon SageMaker.
Encrypt the confidential data in the custom model by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

questions.explanation:
Once a model is trained, confidential data becomes embedded in the model's parameters. The only way to ensure the model does not generate responses based on confidential information is to delete the model, remove sensitive data from the training dataset, and retrain from scratch.

**Learn more:** [Delete a custom model (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-delete.html) · [Data protection (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/data-protection.html)

A publishing company has built a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-based solution that lets users interact with published content. New content is published each day. The company wants to deliver a near-real-time user experience.  
  
Which steps of the RAG pipeline should the company perform using offline batch processing to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Generation of embeddings for user queries

questions.explanation:
Content embeddings and the search index are produced during the data-ingestion phase, before user requests arrive. Batch processing these steps keeps newly published content available for subsequent low-latency query embedding, retrieval, and response generation. AWS guidance describes document embedding and vector-database ingestion as the upfront RAG step, followed by query submission, retrieval, and LLM response generation.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Retrieval Augmented Generation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/retrieval-augmented-generation-options/what-is-rag.html) · [Guidance for Similarity Search-Based Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/similarity-search-based-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-on-aws/)

A company needs to assess AI-generated summaries against reference text. It must measure semantic similarity and coverage of key information.  
  
Which metrics satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
BERTScore measures similarity between generated and reference text using contextual BERT embeddings, enabling semantic comparisons. ROUGE measures overlap with the reference and is recall-oriented, making it suitable for assessing whether a summary covers key reference information.\
\
**Learn more:** [Review metrics for an automated model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-report-programmatic.html)

questions.question:
A company has trained a foundation model (FM) for a specific task. The company must fine-tune the FM to carry out a different but related task.  
  
Which fine-tuning method meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Transfer learning adapts a pretrained model to a new, related task by continuing training with task-specific data, reusing the model’s previously learned representations. AWS documentation identifies fine-tuning of a pretrained model on a new dataset as transfer learning.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to develop a conversational agent. The company needs to prevent the LLM from being manipulated with common prompt engineering techniques to perform undesirable actions or expose sensitive information.  

Which action will reduce these risks?

options.text: Create a prompt template that teaches the LLM to detect attack patterns.
Increase the temperature parameter on invocation requests to the LLM.
Avoid using LLMs that are not listed in Amazon SageMaker.
Decrease the number of input tokens on invocations of the LLM.

questions.explanation:
Creating a prompt template that instructs the LLM to recognize and resist common attack patterns (prompt injection, malicious requests) strengthens the model's ability to defend itself against manipulation. By explicitly teaching the model its boundaries and expected behaviors, you reduce the risk of undesirable outputs and data exposure. Increasing temperature amplifies randomness (counterproductive), restricting to specific platforms lacks security benefit, and limiting input tokens risks losing critical context.

**Learn more:** [Prompt injection security – Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-injection.html) · [Best practices to avoid prompt injection attacks – AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/llm-prompt-engineering-best-practices/best-practices.html)

questions.explanation:

options.text: Configure the application to automatically set the temperature parameter to 0 when submitting the prompt to the LLM.
Configure the application to automatically add
Configure the application to automatically add
Configure the application to automatically set the temperature parameter to 1 when submitting the prompt to the LLM.

questions.explanation:
Temperature is the inference parameter that controls response randomness. A temperature of 0 minimizes randomness and therefore yields the most deterministic and stable output for the same prompt; instructing the model in prompt text does not provide the same sampling control, while a temperature of 1 increases variation.

**Learn more:** [Design a prompt - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/design-a-prompt.html) · [Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial institution is using Amazon Bedrock to develop an AI application. The application is hosted in a VPC. To meet regulatory compliance standards, the VPC is not allowed access to any internet traffic.  

Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink enables private, secure connectivity between VPCs and AWS services without exposing traffic to the public internet. This satisfies regulatory compliance requirements that prohibit internet access while allowing the VPC to access Bedrock and other AWS services over AWS's internal network. Macie provides data security, CloudFront distributes content, and an Internet Gateway provides public internet access—none solve the compliance constraint.

**Learn more:** [Use AWS PrivateLink with Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html) · [Protect your data using Amazon VPC and AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/usingVPC.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is introducing a mobile app that helps users learn foreign languages. The app makes text more coherent by calling a large language model (LLM). The company collected a diverse dataset of text and supplemented the dataset with examples of more readable versions. The company wants the LLM output to resemble the provided examples.  
  
Which metric should the company use to assess whether the LLM meets these requirements?

options.text: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) score

questions.explanation:
ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) is specifically designed to measure how well generated text matches reference examples by calculating n-gram overlap, precision, recall, and F1 scores. Since the company has reference examples of readable text and wants the model's output to resemble them, ROUGE directly evaluates this alignment. The loss function measures training performance, semantic robustness measures resilience, and latency measures speed—none assess output similarity to examples.

**Learn more:** [Use metrics to understand model performance (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-metrics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An AI practitioner is creating a prompt for large language models (LLMs) in Amazon Bedrock. The practitioner must ensure that the prompt works across all Amazon Bedrock LLMs.  
  
Which characteristic may vary among the LLMs?

options.text: The ability to control model output randomness

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock models can have different maximum generated-response token limits. A prompt and its requested output length must therefore remain within the maximum token count supported by every target model. AWS notes that inference-parameter defaults and valid ranges depend on the model, and `maxTokens` defaults to the maximum permitted by the selected model.

**Learn more:** [Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html) · [InferenceConfiguration - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InferenceConfiguration.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a chatbot that uses Amazon Lex and Amazon OpenSearch Service. The chatbot uses the company’s private data to answer questions. The company must convert the data into a vector representation before storing it in a database.  
  
Which type of foundation model (FM) meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
A text embeddings model converts text into numerical vector representations that capture semantic meaning. questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to build a generative AI application by using Amazon Bedrock and needs to choose a foundation model (FM). The company wants to know how much information can fit into one prompt.  

Which consideration will inform the company's decision?
questions.explanation:
The context window defines the maximum number of tokens (input and output combined) a foundation model can process in a single prompt. This directly determines how much information can fit into one prompt. Temperature controls output randomness, batch size relates to throughput efficiency, and model size refers to parameter count—none of these affect individual prompt length limits.

**Learn more:** [Models at a glance - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html) · [Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-supported.html)

questions.question:
A company is using a pre-trained large language model (LLM) to build a chatbot for product recommendations. The company needs the LLM outputs to be short and written in a specific language.  

Which solution will align the LLM response quality with the company's expectations?

options.text: Choose an LLM of a different size.

questions.explanation:
Adjusting the prompt allows direct control over LLM output characteristics including length and language. By crafting instructions like 'Respond in [language] with 2-3 sentences', the model aligns with requirements. Model size, temperature, and top-K control different aspects of generation (creativity, diversity) but do not directly constrain output length or language.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html)

Amazon Bedrock Prompt management lets organizations create and save reusable prompt templates with shared instructions. Variables in the template can be populated at invocation time with each product’s short description, while retaining the common slogan-generation instructions.

**Learn more:** [Construct and store reusable prompts with Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.html) · [Create a prompt using Prompt management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management-create.html)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Which technique can a company use to lower bias and toxicity in generative AI applications during the post-processing ML lifecycle?
questions.explanation:
Human-in-the-loop (HITL) is a post-processing technique where human reviewers evaluate and filter generated outputs to identify and remove biased or toxic content before delivery to end-users. This directly addresses the requirement to reduce bias and toxicity in the post-processing phase. Data augmentation and feature engineering are training-phase techniques, while adversarial training improves model robustness but does not directly filter outputs for toxicity.

**Learn more:** [Considerations for addressing the core dimensions of responsible AI for Amazon Bedrock applications](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/considerations-for-addressing-the-core-dimensions-of-responsible-ai-for-amazon-bedrock-applications/)

questions.question:
A company wants to improve employee productivity by using a generative AI solution to write code for testing software applications.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Q Developer is a managed generative AI assistant for software development that can generate code and unit tests in supported IDEs. It directly supports automated test-code generation without the custom agent implementation required by Amazon Bedrock Agents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Chatting with Amazon Q Developer about code](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/q-in-IDE-chat.html)

questions.question:
A company needs to choose a generative AI model to build an application. The application must return responses to users in real time.  
  
Which model characteristic should the company evaluate to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Inference speed determines how quickly a generative AI model produces responses after receiving user input, making it the relevant characteristic for real-time interactions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Optimize model inference for latency - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/latency-optimized-inference.html)

questions.question:
A company is developing a generative AI tool. The company will use internal documents to customize a foundation model (FM).  
  
Which approach meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Continued pre-training trains a foundation model further on an organization’s unlabeled documents, expanding its domain knowledge and customizing it for that organization’s content. Amazon Bedrock identifies continued pre-training as a model-customization method for using unlabeled data to enhance domain knowledge.\
\
**Learn more:** [AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Generative AI model customization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture-generative-ai/gen-ai-rag.html)

questions.question:
A company uses Amazon Bedrock for a generative AI solution. The solution must integrate with a service that provides vector database storage and vector-search capabilities.  
  
Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon OpenSearch Service supports storing vector embeddings and performing vector similarity searches, and it integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI and knowledge-base workloads. [Vector search – Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/vector-search.html)\
\
**Learn more:** [Vector search – Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/vector-search.html) · [Turning data into a knowledge base – Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-how-data.html)

questions.question:
A retail store wants to predict the demand for a specific product for the next few weeks by using the Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm.  
  
Which type of data will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
The Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm is specifically designed for time series forecasting tasks. It requires historical time-series data (observations collected at regular intervals, such as daily or weekly sales figures) to learn patterns and trends in order to predict future demand values. Text, image, and binary data are not suitable for this algorithm.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use the SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deepar.html)

questions.question:
An ecommerce company wants to group customers according to their purchase history and preferences in order to personalize the user experience in the company’s application.  
  
Which ML technique should the company use?
questions.explanation:
Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning technique that groups customers with similar purchase histories and preferences into segments, enabling personalized application experiences.\
\
**Learn more:** [K-Means Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/k-means.html)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of structured data?

options.text: A file of text comments from an online forum
A compilation of video files that contains news broadcasts
A CSV file that consists of measurement data
Transcribed conversations between call center agents and customers

questions.explanation:
A CSV file organizes measurement values into consistent rows and columns, giving the data a defined tabular structure that can be readily parsed and queried.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is structured data? (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/structured-data/)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
An e-commerce company is deploying a chatbot. The chatbot will allow users to ask questions about the company’s products and receive details about users’ orders. The company must implement safeguards that filter harmful content from input prompts and chatbot responses.  
  
Which AWS feature or resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable content filters that detect and filter harmful content in both user prompts and model-generated responses, making it the appropriate safety control for the chatbot.\
\
**Learn more:** [Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html)

questions.question:
A customer service team is building an application to analyze customer feedback and automatically categorize that feedback. The categories include product quality, customer service, and delivery experience.  
  
Which AI concept does this scenario represent?
questions.explanation:
Natural language processing (NLP) enables systems to interpret, analyze, and classify human-written text, including categorizing customer feedback by its subject or sentiment.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Natural Language Processing? - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/nlp/)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
A financial company wants to create workflows for human review of ML predictions. The company wants to set confidence thresholds for its use case and modify those thresholds over time.  
  
Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) provides human review workflows for machine learning predictions. It supports configuring confidence-based conditions that trigger human review and updating those thresholds as the use case changes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reviewing inappropriate content with Amazon Augmented AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/a2i-rekognition.html) · [Create a Human Review Workflow](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/a2i-create-flow-definition.html)

questions.question:
A financial company wants to create workflows for human review of ML predictions. The company wants to set confidence thresholds for its use case and modify those thresholds over time.  
  
Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Model complexity directly determines how interpretable and explainable AI decisions are. Simpler models like logistic regression or decision trees allow clear tracing of how inputs lead to decisions, making them suitable for high-stakes applications like loan approval where audit trails are critical. More complex models, particularly deep neural networks, function as black boxes and obscure the reasoning behind predictions. Training time, hyperparameter count, and deployment time do not meaningfully affect explainability.

**Learn more:** [Model Explainability with AWS AI/ML Solutions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/model-explainability-aws-ai-ml/model-explainability-aws-ai-ml.html) · [Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-explainability.html)

questions.question:
An AI practitioner needs to evaluate ML models and provide explanations of model predictions to customers and stakeholders.  
  
Which AWS service or feature meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify explains ML model predictions using model-agnostic feature attribution, enabling stakeholders and customers to understand why a model produced a result. It supports both overall model understanding and per-instance prediction explanations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Model Explainability - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-explainability.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
An AI practitioner needs to evaluate ML models and provide explanations of model predictions to customers and stakeholders.  
  
Which AWS service or feature meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Bedrock custom service role for each team that has access to only the team's customer data.
Create a custom service role that has Amazon S3 access. Ask teams to specify the customer name on each Amazon Bedrock request.
Redact personal data in Amazon S3. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow team access to customer data.
Create one Amazon Bedrock role that has full Amazon S3 access. Create IAM roles for each team that have access to only each team's customer folders.

questions.explanation:
Each team requires its own Amazon Bedrock service role with fine-grained permissions restricting access only to that team's customer data folders and resources. This enforces the principle of least privilege at the service level. Creating a single Bedrock role with full S3 access violates security policy; relying on teams to self-specify customer names provides no enforcement mechanism; data redaction alone doesn't solve access control requirements.

**Learn more:** [Service roles for Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-iam-sr.html) · [Identity and access management for Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-iam.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to integrate an AI solution that contacts emergency services within 30 seconds after detecting a vehicle crash. The company intends to use a pre-trained model with no additional training.  
  
Which factor should the company prioritize when choosing a model to satisfy these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Model size directly affects inference latency and compute requirements. Selecting an appropriately smaller pre-trained model helps achieve the strict 30-second response-time requirement without requiring additional training.\
\
**Learn more:** [AI Practitioner exam guide - Domain 3: foundation model selection criteria](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/examguides/ai-practitioner-01-domain3.html) · [Optimize model inference for latency (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/latency-optimized-inference.html)

questions.question:
A healthcare company is developing an AI solution to predict patient readmission within 30 days after discharge. The company has trained a model on historical patient data, including medical history, demographics, and treatment specifications, to generate real-time readmission predictions.  
  
Which task represents AI model inference in this scenario?

options.text: Use appropriate metrics and assess model performance.
Use data to identify patient patterns and correlations.
Use a trained model to predict patient readmission.

questions.explanation:
AI model inference is the use of a trained machine-learning model with input data to generate a prediction or output. Applying the trained model to patient data to predict readmission is therefore inference.\
\
**Learn more:** [Run AI/ML inference workloads on Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/ml-inference.html)

questions.question: Which technique trains AI models using labeled datasets to adapt them to particular industry terminology and requirements?
questions.explanation:
Fine-tuning further trains a pretrained model on labeled domain- or task-specific examples, enabling it to learn specialized terminology and meet particular requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-fine-tuning.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to improve its chatbot responses so they align with the company’s desired tone. The company has 100 examples of high-quality conversations between customer service agents and customers. The company wants to use this data to incorporate the company tone into the chatbot’s responses.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Personalize to generate responses.
Create an Amazon SageMaker HyperPod pre-training job.
Host the model by using Amazon SageMaker. Use TensorRT for large language model (LLM) deployment.
Create an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning creates a customized model by training a foundation model on the company’s example conversations, allowing the model to learn the desired response style and tone. AWS documents that a fine-tuning job customizes a base model using specified training data.

**Learn more:** [CreateModelCustomizationJob - Amazon Bedrock API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_CreateModelCustomizationJob.html) · [Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-fine-tuning.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use a pre-trained generative AI model to generate content for its marketing campaigns. The company needs to ensure that the generated content aligns with the company's brand voice and messaging requirements.  

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Optimize the model's architecture and hyperparameters to improve the model's overall performance.
Increase the model's complexity by adding more layers to the model's architecture.
Create effective prompts that provide clear instructions and context to guide the model's generation.
Select a large, diverse dataset to pre-train a new generative model.

questions.explanation:
Prompt engineering—crafting detailed prompts with clear instructions and context—is the most effective way to guide a pre-trained model to generate content aligned with brand voice and messaging without modifying the underlying model.

**Learn more:** [Prompt engineering concepts (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to choose a model from Amazon Bedrock to use internally. The company must identify a model that generates responses in a style that the company's employees prefer.  

What should the company do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Evaluate the models by using built-in prompt datasets.
Evaluate the models by using a human workforce and custom prompt datasets.
Use public model leaderboards to identify the model.
Use the model InvocationLatency runtime metrics in Amazon CloudWatch when trying models.

questions.explanation:
Evaluating models with human workforce and custom prompt datasets tailored to the company's specific needs ensures the selected model matches employee preferences for response style. Generic built-in datasets or public leaderboards cannot measure subjective alignment with internal requirements.

**Learn more:** [Model evaluation jobs that use human workers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-type-human.html) · [Evaluate the performance of Amazon Bedrock resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/evaluation.html)

questions.question:
A human resources company is developing an AI/ML solution to screen resumes and choose relevant applicants for various job roles.  
  
Which AI methodologies can help ensure impartial treatment of all demographic groups? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Fairness evaluates and mitigates biased model outcomes across demographic groups. Explainability makes selection decisions interpretable and auditable, which helps detect and address discriminatory factors or proxies in the screening process.\
\
**Learn more:** [Responsible AI - Generative AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/responsible-ai.html) · [Core dimensions of responsible AI](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/considerations-for-addressing-the-core-dimensions-of-responsible-ai-for-amazon-bedrock-applications/)

questions.question:
A human resources company is developing an AI/ML solution to screen resumes and choose relevant applicants for various job roles.  
  
Which AI methodologies can help ensure impartial treatment of all demographic groups? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use data from only customers who match the demographics of the company's overall customer base.
Collect data from customers who have a past purchase history.
Ensure that the data is balanced and collected from a diverse group.
Ensure that the data is from a publicly available dataset.

questions.explanation:
Balanced data collected from a diverse, representative group helps prevent systematic overrepresentation or underrepresentation of customer groups, reducing the risk of biased model outcomes. Microsoft guidance identifies diverse and representative training data as a fairness practice to minimize bias.

**Learn more:** [Apply responsible AI principles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/microsoft-copilot-studio/guidance/responsible-ai) · [Understand your datasets - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/concept-data-analysis?view=azureml-api-2)

Negative prompts explicitly specify what should not be included in the generated images, helping the model focus on desired attributes and filter out unrelated content. This technique directly addresses the problem of random or irrelevant image generation by constraining the output space. Zero-shot and positive prompts alone provide less explicit guidance on what to avoid, while ambiguous prompts would worsen the issue.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Titan Image Generator model parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-titan-image.html) · [Stability AI models on Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-stability-diffusion.html)

Which situation illustrates a possible risk and limitation of prompt engineering when using a generative AI model?

options.text: Prompt engineering does not ensure that the model always produces consistent and deterministic outputs, eliminating the need for validation.
Prompt engineering could expose the model to vulnerabilities such as prompt injection attacks.
Properly designed prompts reduce but do not eliminate the risk of data poisoning or model hijacking.
Prompt engineering does not ensure that the model will consistently generate highly reliable outputs when working with real-world data.

questions.explanation:
Prompt injection is a security vulnerability in which malicious instructions embedded in user-controlled or external content attempt to override intended model behavior. Prompt engineering alone cannot guarantee protection against these attacks.

**Learn more:** [Prompt injection security (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-injection.html) · [Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-prompt-attack.html)

questions.question: Which choice is an example of unsupervised learning?

options.text: Clustering data points into groups based on their similarity
Training a model to recognize images of animals
Predicting the price of a house based on the house’s features
Generating human-like text based on a given prompt

questions.explanation:
Unsupervised learning discovers structure in unlabeled data. Clustering organizes data points into similarity-based groups without requiring known output labels.\
\
**Learn more:** [Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/compare/the-difference-between-machine-learning-supervised-and-unsupervised/)

questions.question:
An ecommerce company uses a generative AI chatbot to answer customer inquiries. The company wants to measure the chatbot’s financial impact on its operations.  
  
Which metric should the company use?
questions.explanation:
Cost for each customer conversation directly measures the operational cost of serving customers through the chatbot and supports evaluation of its financial impact.\
\
**Learn more:** [Generative AI pricing model (AWS Well-Architected)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/gencost02.html) · [Optimizing costs of generative AI applications on AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/optimizing-costs-of-generative-ai-applications-on-aws/)

Which prompting attack directly exposes the configured behavior of a large language model (LLM)?
questions.explanation:
Extracting the prompt template is a prompting attack that directly reveals the underlying configured behavior, instructions, or system prompts of an LLM. This exposes how the model has been configured and designed to respond, giving attackers insight into the model's constraints and behavioral instructions. The other options involve manipulating the model's behavior (persona switches, friendliness exploitation) or ignoring prompts, but they do not directly expose the configured behavior itself.

**Learn more:** [LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage - OWASP Gen AI Security Project](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm07-insecure-plugin-design/) · [Designing for the inevitable: system prompt leakage and mitigations](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/designing-for-the-inevitable-system-prompt-leakage-and-mitigations-in-generative-ai-applications/)

questions.question:
A company wants to create an application by using Amazon Bedrock. The company has a limited budget and prefers flexibility without long-term commitment.  

Which Amazon Bedrock pricing model meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
On-Demand pricing for Amazon Bedrock requires no long-term commitment and charges only for actual usage, providing maximum flexibility and cost control for companies with limited budgets and variable workloads. Model customization is a feature, not a pricing model. Provisioned Throughput requires capacity reservations (long-term commitment), and Spot Instance is an EC2 concept not applicable to Bedrock.\
\
**Learn more:** [Amazon Bedrock pricing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/bedrock-pricing.html) · [Amazon Bedrock Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/)

questions.question: Which technique divides a complex task into smaller subtasks that are submitted sequentially to a large language model (LLM)?
questions.explanation:
Prompt chaining breaks a complex workflow into sequential subtasks, with each LLM output able to inform the next prompt in the chain.\
\
**Learn more:** [Perform AI prompt-chaining with Amazon Bedrock (Step Functions)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/sample-bedrock-prompt-chaining.html) · [Build and orchestrate generative AI applications with Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/bedrock-runtime_example_cross_ServerlessPromptChaining_section.html)

Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate temporary credentials for model use.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A healthcare company needs to analyze patient data. The data was collected during the previous year to identify patterns in disease outbreaks. The company must produce a monthly trend-analysis report to present to public health officials. It must also provide insights from patient data for the most recent month of the current year.  
  
Which inference method will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?
questions.explanation:
Batch transform is designed for offline inference over an entire dataset and does not require a continuously running endpoint. It is well suited to scheduled monthly trend analysis of historical patient data, making it more cost-effective than inference methods intended for low-latency or continuously available predictions.

**Learn more:** [Batch transform for inference - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-transform.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is implementing intelligent agents to provide conversational search experiences for its customers. The company needs a database service that will support storage and queries of embeddings from a generative AI model as vectors in the database.  
  
Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL supports the pgvector extension, which enables efficient storage and similarity-based queries of vector embeddings. This is essential for conversational search and intelligent agent systems that leverage embeddings from generative AI models. Amazon Athena is a query service without vector support, Redshift is for data warehousing, and EMR is for distributed processing—none provide native vector database functionality.

**Learn more:** [Using Aurora PostgreSQL as a Knowledge Base for Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.VectorDB.html) · [Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL pgvector support](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2023/07/amazon-aurora-postgresql-pgvector-vector-storage-similarity-search/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An education provider is building a question and answer application that uses a generative AI model to explain complex concepts. The education provider wants to automatically change the style of the model response depending on who is asking the question. The education provider will give the model the age range of the user who has asked the question.  

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

options.text: Fine-tune the model by using additional training data that is representative of the various age ranges that the application will support.
Add a role description to the prompt context that instructs the model of the age range that the response should target.
Use chain-of-thought reasoning to deduce the correct style and complexity for a response suitable for that user.
Summarize the response text depending on the age of the user so that younger users receive shorter responses.

questions.explanation:
Prompt engineering with role descriptions requires minimal implementation effort—adding context like "explain this concept for a 10-year-old" to the prompt guides the model to adjust tone and complexity automatically. This leverages the model's existing capabilities without retraining. Fine-tuning requires substantial labeled data and compute; chain-of-thought reasoning adds inference time without ensuring appropriateness; post-hoc response summarization is less direct.

**Learn more:** [Prompt engineering concepts (persona/role) - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html)

Threat detection and data protection are the two capabilities directly aligned with regulatory compliance frameworks. Threat detection (e.g., AWS GuardDuty) identifies unauthorized access and attacks, while data protection via encryption and access controls safeguards sensitive customer information. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial company is building a generative AI application to make loan-approval decisions. The company requires the application's output to be responsible and fair.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

Use a deep learning model with many hidden layers.
Keep the model’s decision-making process a secret to protect proprietary algorithms.

questions.question:
A company wants to build an interpretable ML model to evaluate the risk of loan applications.  
  
Which ML model type or algorithm meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Logistic regression is an interpretable supervised model for binary outcomes such as loan risk. Its feature coefficients show the direction and relative influence of each input on the predicted probability, supporting transparent risk assessments.\
\
**Learn more:** [Linear Learner Algorithm (Amazon SageMaker)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/linear-learner.html) · [Interpretability on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/ml-model-interpretability/sagemaker.html)

Which ML model type or algorithm meets these requirements?

options.text: Evaluate the model's performance on benchmark datasets.
Analyze the model's architecture and hyperparameters.
Assess the model's alignment with specific use cases.
Measure the computational resources required for model deployment.

questions.explanation:
To determine if a foundation model meets business objectives, it must be assessed for alignment with specific use cases and real-world applications relevant to the business. This direct evaluation ensures the model produces valuable, actionable outputs for the organization's goals. While benchmark performance (A), architecture analysis (B), and resource measurement (D) are useful, they do not directly validate whether the model solves the intended business problem.

**Learn more:** [What are foundation model evaluations?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-foundation-model-evaluate-whatis.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company intends to use a generative AI model to deliver real-time service quotes to users.  
  
Which criterion should the company use to choose the correct model for this use case?

options.text: General-purpose use and high-powered GPU availability
Model latency and optimized inference speed

questions.explanation:
Real-time generative AI applications require low-latency responses. Model latency and optimized inference speed determine whether service quotes can be generated quickly enough for an interactive user experience. AWS guidance identifies inference latency as critical for real-time applications.

**Learn more:** [Performance efficiency - Generative AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/performance-efficiency.html) · [Choosing models for generative AI applications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/gen-ai-lifecycle-operational-excellence/dev-experimenting-model-selection.html)

questions.question: What does an F1 score evaluate in the context of foundation model (FM) performance?

options.text: Financial cost of operating the model
Energy efficiency of the model’s computations

questions.explanation:
An F1 score combines precision and recall through their harmonic mean, measuring how well predictions balance correctness among positive predictions with coverage of actual positive cases.\
\
**Learn more:** [Metrics and validation (Amazon SageMaker Autopilot)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-metrics-validation.html) · [Binary Model Insights (Amazon Machine Learning)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/binary-model-insights.html)

questions.question: What does an F1 score evaluate in the context of foundation model (FM) performance?

options.text: Include more diverse training data. Fine-tune the model again by using the new data.
Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with the fine-tuned model.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor checks to eliminate bias.
Pre-train a new LLM with more diverse training data.

questions.explanation:
The demographic disparity in loan approvals most likely stems from an unrepresentative training set, so augmenting the data with more diverse examples and re-fine-tuning the existing model directly targets the root cause at a fraction of the cost of pre-training a brand-new foundation model. Retrieval Augmented Generation only supplements the model's context at inference time and does not correct bias already learned in the model's weights, and AWS Trusted Advisor has no capability to detect or remediate model bias.

**Learn more:** [Pre-training data bias - SageMaker Clarify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-detect-data-bias.html) · [Responsible AI dimensions (AWS Well-Architected)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/responsible-ai.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a new generative AI chatbot. The chatbot uses an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) to generate responses. During testing, the company finds that the chatbot is susceptible to prompt injection attacks.

Use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails content filters and denied topics.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to fine-tune a foundation model (FM) to answer questions in a particular domain. The company intends to use instruction-based fine-tuning.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to make a chatbot to help customers. The chatbot will help solve technical problems without human intervention.

Use batch inferencing to process detailed responses.

A company is developing a chatbot that uses a large language model (LLM) to respond to customer product questions. The company wants the chatbot to answer product questions only and not respond to questions about any other topics.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set guardrails on the LLM prompt template.
Write custom application logic to identify questions about other topics.
Reduce the information the LLM can access.
Set the temperature parameter value to a lower number.

questions.explanation:
LLM guardrails can define and block undesirable or denied topics in user inputs and model responses, providing managed enforcement of a product-only scope. Custom application logic requires ongoing development and maintenance; restricting information access does not prevent responses based on the model’s general knowledge, and temperature controls randomness rather than topic boundaries.

**Learn more:** [Block denied topics to help remove harmful content - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-denied-topics.html) · [Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html)

questions.question:
A company plans to use foundation models (FMs) to build and deploy an AI model.  
  
Which AWS service or resource satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** development effort?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that provides access to foundation models through APIs and enables organizations to build, integrate, and deploy generative AI applications without training models from scratch or managing underlying infrastructure.\

questions.question:

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Modify the advanced prompts for the agent to include the examples.
Create a guardrail for the agent that includes the examples.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label the examples.
Run a script in AWS Lambda that adds the examples to the training dataset.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Agents advanced prompt templates support hand-curated examples for few-shot prompting, which improves model accuracy for a specific task. Adding the examples to the agent’s advanced prompts therefore meets the requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enhance agent accuracy using advanced prompt templates in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompts.html)

questions.question:
A company is building an agent for its application using Amazon Bedrock Agents. The agent is performing well, but the company wants to improve the agent’s accuracy by supplying specific examples.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Expanding initiatives across business units to create long-term business value
Ensuring alignment with business standards, revenue goals, and stakeholder expectations
Overcoming challenges to drive business transformation and growth
Developing policies and guidelines for data, transparency, responsible AI, and compliance

questions.explanation:
AI governance frameworks define policies and guidelines that govern data practices, transparency, responsible AI, accountability, and compliance. These controls help ensure that AI systems are trustworthy, ethical, and human-centered throughout their lifecycle.

**Learn more:** [Govern AI — Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ai/govern) · [Guidance to set your organization's responsible AI policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ai/responsible-ai-policies)

questions.question:
A company has developed multiple ML models. The company requires a solution to store, manage, and version the models.  
  
Which AWS service or feature satisfies these requirements?

Amazon SageMaker Model Registry catalogs ML models and manages their versions, metadata, lifecycle stages, and approval status through model groups and versioned model packages.\
\
**Learn more:** [Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-registry.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to use AI for budgeting. It created one budget manually and another by using an AI model. The company compared the budgets to assess the AI model’s performance. The AI-model budget contained incorrect numbers.  
  
Which option represents the AI model’s problem?
questions.explanation:
Hallucinations occur when an AI model generates incorrect or fabricated information, such as inaccurate budget figures.\
\
**Learn more:** [Minimize generative AI hallucinations with Automated Reasoning checks (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/minimize-generative-ai-hallucinations-with-amazon-bedrock-automated-reasoning-checks/)

questions.question: What is the main purpose of system prompts in generative AI applications?

options.text: To authenticate user credentials to access responses from AI
To generate random responses by AI
To define the role and behavioral boundaries of AI
To compress output data from AI

questions.explanation:
System prompts establish the AI system’s role, instructions, behavioral constraints, and response boundaries, guiding how it should handle subsequent requests.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prompt engineering concepts (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html) · [Configure advanced prompts (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/configure-advanced-prompts.html)

questions.question: What is the main purpose of system prompts in generative AI applications?
questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail logs all API requests to Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services, providing comprehensive audit trails. For 5-year retention at the lowest cost, Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically transitions logs between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing costs over time. CloudWatch (B) is for monitoring, Audit Manager (C) is for compliance management, and S3 Standard (E) lacks the cost optimization of Intelligent-Tiering.

questions.question: Which phase of the ML lifecycle determines compliance and regulatory requirements?
questions.explanation:

At this stage, organizations define project scope and constraints, including legal obligations (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.), ethical considerations, and industry-specific regulations. These requirements then inform all subsequent phases. While data collection involves compliance execution, the strategic determination of what regulations apply occurs at project initiation.\
\
**Learn more:** [ML lifecycle phase - Business goal identification - Machine Learning Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/ml-lifecycle-phase-business-goal.html)

Which solution fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Analyze cost and usage reports in AWS Cost Explorer.
Download AWS security and compliance documents from AWS Artifact.
Configure Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to restrict discoverable FMs.
Build a hybrid search solution by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart can use private curated model hubs to limit employees to approved subsets of publicly available foundation models. These hubs enforce organization-level access controls and improve discoverability of the permitted models.\

questions.question: Which prompting technique can protect against prompt injection attacks?
questions.explanation:
Adversarial prompting involves deliberately crafting potentially harmful prompts to expose vulnerabilities and weaknesses in an AI system's safety mechanisms. This proactive security testing approach helps identify and remediate susceptibilities to prompt injection attacks before deployment. Zero-shot prompting is a simple query technique unrelated to security, least-to-most prompting simplifies task complexity, and chain-of-thought prompting improves reasoning but is not a primary defense against injection attacks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Adversarial Prompting in LLMs - Prompt Engineering Guide](https://www.promptingguide.ai/risks/adversarial)

questions.question:
An AI practitioner has trained a model using a training dataset. The model performs well on the training data; however, it does not perform well on evaluation data.  
  
What is the **MOST** likely cause of this issue?
questions.explanation:
Overfitting occurs when a model fits the training data very closely, including patterns that do not generalize to unseen evaluation data. It therefore performs well during training but poorly on evaluation data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Model Fit: Underfitting vs. Overfitting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/model-fit-underfitting-vs-overfitting.html) · [What is Overfitting?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/overfitting/)

questions.question:
A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to produce article summaries in multiple languages. The company requires a metric to assess the quality of those summary translations across multiple languages.  
  
Which evaluation metric meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
BLEU evaluates machine translation quality by measuring n-gram overlap between generated text and reference translations. AWS documentation identifies BLEU as commonly used for translation evaluation; ROUGE is chiefly a summarization metric, while AUC and precision assess classification performance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Evaluating your SageMaker AI-trained model - Amazon Nova](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-model-evaluation.html)

Named entity recognition identifies specific entities like names and dates but does not provide comprehensive key point extraction; recommendation engines and translation systems are unrelated to the stated requirement.\

questions.question: Which AWS service offers a broad selection of high-performing generative AI foundation models (FMs)?

Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed AWS service that provides secure access to high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies for building generative AI applications.\

How can companies use large language models (LLMs) securely on Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: Design clear and specific prompts. Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and policies by using least privilege access.
Enable AWS Audit Manager for automatic model evaluation jobs.
Enable Amazon Bedrock automatic model evaluation jobs.
Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to make models explainable and to monitor for bias.

questions.explanation:

The other options (Audit Manager, automatic evaluation jobs, CloudWatch Logs) address monitoring or auditing, not security controls.

**Learn more:** [Identity and access management for Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-iam.html) · [Implementing least privilege access for Amazon Bedrock – AWS Security Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/implementing-least-privilege-access-for-amazon-bedrock/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has built an image classification model to predict plant diseases from photos of plant leaves. The company wants to evaluate how many images the model classified correctly.  

Which evaluation metric should the company use to measure the model's performance?
questions.explanation:
Accuracy measures the proportion of correctly classified instances out of all instances, making it the ideal metric for evaluating how many images a classification model predicted correctly. This metric is straightforward and directly answers the business question when classes are reasonably balanced. R-squared and RMSE are regression metrics, while learning rate is a hyperparameter, not an evaluation metric.

**Learn more:** [Evaluating model accuracy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/evaluating-model-accuracy.html) · [SageMaker classification metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-metrics-validation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has documents that are missing some words because of a database error. The company wants to build an ML model that can suggest potential words to fill in the missing text.  

Which type of model meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
BERT-based models excel at predicting masked words in text through bidirectional context understanding—a technique called masked language modeling. This makes them ideally suited for text completion and word prediction tasks. Other options fail: topic modeling categorizes documents but doesn't predict words; clustering groups data without generating predictions; prescriptive models recommend actions rather than fill text.

**Learn more:** [Masked language modeling – Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/tasks/masked_language_modeling) · [Deploy a BERT model for Fill-Mask on Amazon SageMaker (AWS Samples)](https://github.com/aws-samples/amazon-sagemaker-hugging-face-bert-model-fill-mask)

Using a diverse dataset of insect bite images across different genders, ethnicities, and geographic locations demonstrates the principle of fairness in responsible AI. Use Amazon Rekognition to optimize the model.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],What is continued pre-training?

questions.question:
A company trains ML models using datasets in which some classes contain more examples than others. The company wants to assess how effectively the model balances detecting and labeling the classes.  
  
Which metric should the company use?
questions.explanation:
F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, measuring the balance between finding instances of a class and assigning correct class labels. It is especially useful when class frequencies are imbalanced, where accuracy alone can be misleading.\
\
**Learn more:** [Metrics and validation (Amazon SageMaker Autopilot)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-metrics-validation.html)

questions.question:
A company trains ML models using datasets in which some classes contain more examples than others. The company wants to assess how effectively the model balances detecting and labeling the classes.  
  
Which metric should the company use?
questions.explanation:
Data augmentation for imbalanced classes addresses bias in image generation models by artificially increasing the diversity and representation of underrepresented groups or attributes in the training data. By applying transformations (rotations, color jittering, etc.) to expand minority class samples, the model learns more fairly across demographic groups. Model monitoring detects bias post-training, RAG is for retrieval tasks, and watermark detection verifies image provenance—none directly mitigate training data bias.

**Learn more:** [Balance your data for machine learning with Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/balance-your-data-for-machine-learning-with-amazon-sagemaker-data-wrangler/) · [Class Imbalance (CI) – Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-bias-metric-class-imbalance.html)

options.text: Run batch inference jobs on the unlabeled data.

Use an optical character recognition model trained on labeled samples to label unlabeled samples.
Run an Amazon SageMaker AI labeling job.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth labeling jobs can use Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate human labels, provided the data is appropriate for a public workforce. questions.question:

Which AI risk does this represent?
questions.explanation:
Nondeterminism is output variability: the same model input can yield different generated responses across runs. A deterministic model, by contrast, always produces the same output for the same input.\
\

questions.question:

options.text: Include demographically diverse data sources to improve model fairness.
Apply consistent labeling standards across the training dataset.
Focus exclusively on high-volume data regardless of quality.
Use only synthetic data to train the model.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an ML model to predict customer churn. The model performs well on the training dataset but does not accurately predict churn for new data.  
  
Which solution will resolve this issue?

options.text: Decrease the regularization parameter to increase model complexity.
Increase the regularization parameter to decrease model complexity.
Add more features to the input data.
Train the model for more epochs.

questions.explanation:
When a model performs well on training data but poorly on new data, it exhibits overfitting. Increasing the regularization parameter penalizes model complexity, reducing the number of features the model relies on and encouraging it to capture general patterns rather than noise. This improves generalization to unseen data. Decreasing regularization or adding more features would worsen overfitting, and additional training epochs would likely reinforce the overfit.

**Learn more:** [What is Overfitting? - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/overfitting/) · [Tune a linear learner model - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/linear-learner-tuning.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A security company uses Amazon Bedrock to run foundation models (FMs). lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) on Amazon Bedrock for sentiment analysis. The company needs the LLM to produce more consistent responses to the same input prompt.  

Which adjustment to an inference parameter should the company make to meet these requirements?

options.text: Decrease the length of output tokens.

questions.explanation:
The temperature parameter controls randomness in LLM outputs: lower values (approaching 0) make predictions deterministic and consistent, while higher values introduce creativity and variation. For sentiment analysis requiring reliable, repeatable responses to identical prompts, decreasing temperature is the appropriate adjustment. The other parameters affect output length or training behavior rather than consistency.

questions.explanation:
BLEU measures the similarity between machine-translated output and high-quality reference translations by comparing matching n-grams. Using the same document corpus and human responses as references enables BLEU scores to compare the translation tool’s quality relative to the human method; BLEU does not provide a reliable absolute measure of translation quality across contexts.

**Learn more:** [The BLEU translation quality metric](https://docs.cloud.google.com/translate/docs/bleu-scores)

questions.question:
A company needs to detect unauthorized API activity for foundation models (FMs) in Amazon Bedrock.  
  
Which solution fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail to monitor API activity.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to monitor model input and output data.
Create Amazon QuickSight dashboards to monitor row-level safety.
Monitor user access by using Amazon Personalize.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail records Amazon Bedrock API calls as events and includes details such as the requesting identity, source IP address, time, and requested action. These audit records can be monitored and analyzed to identify unauthorized API activity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Monitor Amazon Bedrock API calls using CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/logging-using-cloudtrail.html)

A company needs to fine-tune an ML model hosted on Amazon Bedrock. The company plans to use its own sensitive data, which is stored in private databases in a VPC. The data must remain inside the company’s private network.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Restrict access to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) service role.
Restrict access to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resource policy.
Use AWS PrivateLink to connect the VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt the data.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink provides an interface VPC endpoint that privately connects a VPC to Amazon Bedrock, allowing Bedrock API access without an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, or public IP addresses. IAM policies control permissions and AWS KMS encrypts data, but neither provides the required private network connectivity.

**Learn more:** [Use interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to create a private connection between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question: Which Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) can be fine-tuned for comprehension of text, images, and video?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Nova Pro is a fine-tunable multimodal model that accepts text, image, and video inputs, enabling customization for comprehension tasks across all three modalities.\
\
**Learn more:** [Nova Pro - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-amazon-nova-pro.html) · [Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-fine-tuning.html)

questions.question:
An AI practitioner uses Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to build a reusable prompt. The prompt must be capable of interacting with external services by calling an external API.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A tools configuration defines the tools a compatible model can use while generating a response, enabling the model to invoke an external API capability. Prompt variables provide value substitution, and stop sequences only determine when generation stops.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a prompt using Prompt management - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management-create.html)

questions.question:
An animation company needs to provide subtitles for its content.  
  
Which AWS service fulfills this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Transcribe automatically converts spoken audio to text and can generate video subtitle files in WebVTT or SubRip formats.\
\
**Learn more:** [Creating video subtitles - Amazon Transcribe](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/subtitles.html)

questions.question: Which machine learning technique uses training data labeled with the correct output values?
questions.explanation:
Supervised learning trains a model on input examples paired with their known correct output values (labels).\
\
**Learn more:** [Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/compare/the-difference-between-machine-learning-supervised-and-unsupervised/)

questions.question:
A company wants to invoke one Amazon Bedrock endpoint and requires Amazon Bedrock to select the most appropriate foundation model (FM) for each request. The company does not want to hardcode a model.  
  
Which Amazon Bedrock feature or resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock prompt routing provides one serverless endpoint that dynamically routes each request to a suitable foundation model based on its routing criteria and predicted response quality. It eliminates the need for application-side model-selection logic.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understanding intelligent prompt routing in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-routing.html)

questions.question:
A company’s large language model (LLM) is experiencing hallucinations.  
  
How can the company reduce hallucinations?

options.text: Set up Agents for Amazon Bedrock to supervise the model training.
Use data pre-processing and remove any data that causes hallucinations.
Decrease the temperature inference parameter for the model.
Use a foundation model (FM) that is trained to not hallucinate.

questions.explanation:
A lower temperature inference setting reduces randomness by favoring higher-probability token choices, producing more deterministic and predictable model responses. This can reduce hallucinated outputs, although it does not eliminate them entirely.\
\
**Learn more:** [Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html)

questions.question:
A company’s large language model (LLM) is experiencing hallucinations.  
  
How can the company reduce hallucinations?

options.text: A process that uses large amounts of new data to train large language models (LLMs) to improve LLM performance
A process by which large language models (LLMs) reference external authoritative knowledge bases to enhance the relevance and accuracy of LLM responses without re-training
A process that limits large language models (LLMs) exclusively to their original training data to improve response speed for business applications without re-training
A process that focuses on language translation tasks for businesses that operate in multiple countries

questions.explanation:
Retrieval Augmented Generation retrieves relevant content from external, authoritative knowledge bases and incorporates it into a model’s response generation. It can improve relevance and factual accuracy without retraining the large language model.

**Learn more:** [What is RAG? (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed an ML model and wants to give external customers secure access to it through the customers’ own applications.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a custom script in the customers' application for authentication.
Store model credentials and share them with the customers directly for authentication.
Create a secure API endpoint that customers can use.
Embed the model directly into the customers' applications.

questions.explanation:
A secure API endpoint exposes the model’s inference capability while keeping the model and its credentials under company control. The endpoint can enforce authentication and authorization for each customer application and protect requests in transit. Amazon API Gateway, for example, supports access-control mechanisms such as JWT authorizers, Lambda authorizers, and IAM authorization for HTTP APIs.

**Learn more:** [Control and manage access to HTTP APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-access-control.html)
