questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to enhance a large language model (LLM) for content moderation within 3 months. The company wants the model to moderate content in accordance with the company's values and ethics. The LLM must also be capable of handling emerging trends and new forms of problematic content.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Conduct continuous pre-training on a large amount of text-based internet content.
Create a high quality dataset of historical moderation decisions.
Fine-tune the LLM on a diverse set of general ethical guidelines from various sources.
Conduct reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) by using real-time input from skilled moderators.

questions.explanation:
Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) aligns model behavior with human preferences by using feedback in the reward signal. Real-time feedback from skilled moderators can express the company’s moderation values and continually incorporate newly emerging forms of problematic content.

**Learn more:** [Data lifecycle in generative AI - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/strategy-data-considerations-gen-ai/lifecycle.html) · [Customize a model with reinforcement fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/reinforcement-fine-tuning.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A documentary filmmaker wants to reach a larger audience. They want to automatically add subtitles and voice-overs in multiple languages to their films.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Translate to generate subtitles in other languages.
Use Amazon Textract and Amazon Translate to generate subtitles in other languages.
Use Amazon Polly to generate voice-overs in other languages.
Use Amazon Translate to generate voice-overs in other languages.
Use Amazon Textract to generate voice-overs in other languages.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Transcribe provides speech-to-text and subtitle output for media, while Amazon Translate translates the resulting text into other languages. Amazon Polly converts translated text into lifelike speech, enabling voice-overs in the target languages. Amazon Textract is for extracting text from documents and images, and Amazon Translate is a text-translation service rather than a speech-synthesis service.

**Learn more:** [Creating video subtitles - Amazon Transcribe](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/subtitles.html) · [What is Amazon Translate?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/translate/latest/dg/what-is.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A social media company uses an AI-based **“Add as Friend”** recommendation system. The company wants to make sure its AI models are transparent and explainable.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient way?

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze user profile pictures to improve model recommendations.
Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to enhance the explainability of model recommendations.
Migrate the AI model to Amazon Personalize to improve model recommendations.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to manually detect model bias.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify provides managed model-explainability capabilities, including feature attributions that show how input features contributed to individual predictions and overall model behavior. This directly supports transparent, interpretable recommendation outcomes without building a separate explanation system.

A company has fine-tuned a large language model (LLM) to answer questions for a help desk. The company wants to determine if the fine-tuning has enhanced the model's accuracy.

questions.explanation:

Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock provide built-in safety mechanisms and content filtering policies that prevent inappropriate topics and ensure generated content adheres to age-appropriate guidelines. For a children's storytelling application, guardrails automatically block harmful, explicit, or unsuitable content before delivery. Rekognition is for image analysis; playgrounds are testing environments; agents are for multi-step workflows.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to build AI/ML solutions. The company must use only approved data to train models. The AI/ML solutions must comply with company policy and ethical guidelines.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Catalog enables secure discovery and access to approved data and AI assets, with governance-oriented publishing and subscription workflows. It therefore supports restricting model training to approved data while enforcing organizational data and AI governance requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Amazon SageMaker?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/next-generation-sagemaker/latest/userguide/what-is-sagemaker.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
A company uses Amazon SageMaker AI to build AI/ML solutions. The company must use only approved data to train models. The AI/ML solutions must comply with company policy and ethical guidelines.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock with Provisioned Throughput.
Use Amazon Bedrock with On-Demand Throughput.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock On-Demand Throughput is appropriate for an unpredictable, low-volume generative-AI workload because it does not require provisioned compute capacity and charges only for usage. Provisioned Throughput incurs hourly charges for dedicated model capacity and is intended when predictable throughput is needed. [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-use.html)

**Learn more:** [Set up inference for a custom model - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-use.html) · [Increase model invocation capacity with Provisioned Throughput in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-throughput.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to train an ML model to classify images of different types of animals. The company has a large dataset of labeled images and will not label more data.  
  
Which type of learning should the company use to train the model?
questions.explanation:
Supervised learning is the appropriate choice when training an image classifier with a large dataset of labeled images. In supervised learning, input-output pairs (images and corresponding animal classes) enable the model to learn discriminative patterns. Unsupervised learning (B) requires unlabeled data, reinforcement learning (C) uses reward signals, and active learning (D) requires iterative labeling—all misaligned with having a complete labeled dataset.

**Learn more:** [Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning](https://aws.amazon.com/compare/the-difference-between-machine-learning-supervised-and-unsupervised/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A research company implemented a chatbot by using a foundation model (FM) from Amazon Bedrock. The chatbot searches for answers to questions from a large database of research papers.  

After multiple prompt engineering attempts, the company notices that the FM is performing poorly because of the complex scientific terms in the research papers.  

How can the company improve the performance of the chatbot?

options.text: Use few-shot prompting to define how the FM can answer the questions.
Use domain adaptation fine-tuning to adapt the FM to complex scientific terms.
Clean the research paper data to remove complex scientific terms.

questions.explanation:
Domain adaptation fine-tuning customizes a foundation model on a specialized dataset (research papers with complex scientific terminology) to improve its understanding and handling of domain-specific language. Since multiple prompt engineering attempts have already been tried without sufficient improvement, fine-tuning is the appropriate next step. Few-shot prompting alone cannot overcome structural limitations; parameter adjustment and data cleaning do not add domain knowledge.

**Learn more:** [Customize models in Amazon Bedrock with fine-tuning and continued pre-training](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/customize-models-in-amazon-bedrock-with-your-own-data-using-fine-tuning-and-continued-pre-training/) · [Supported models for fine-tuning and continued pre-training](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-supported.html)

questions.question: Which term describes the speed at which a pre-trained foundation model (FM) handles requests and produces output?
questions.explanation:
Inference latency is the time a model takes to generate a response to a prompt, so it measures request-processing and output-delivery speed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Performance efficiency – Generative AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/performance-efficiency.html)

questions.question: Which term describes the speed at which a pre-trained foundation model (FM) handles requests and produces output?

options.text: Train the model by using context data.
Pre-train and benchmark the model by using context data.
Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with prompt engineering techniques.

questions.explanation:
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant, up-to-date content from a knowledge source and adds it to the model prompt when generating an answer. Updating the FAQ content does not require retraining or fine-tuning the model, making it well suited and more cost-effective for changing question-and-answer knowledge.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-how-it-works.html) · [Generative AI options for querying custom documents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/retrieval-augmented-generation-options/options.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a custom AI solution in Amazon SageMaker Studio to analyze financial transactions for fraudulent activity in real time. The company must ensure that connectivity from SageMaker Studio to Amazon Bedrock passes through the company’s VPC.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and policies for SageMaker Studio to access Amazon Bedrock.
Configure Amazon Macie to proxy requests from SageMaker Studio to Amazon Bedrock.
Configure AWS PrivateLink endpoints for the Amazon Bedrock API endpoints in the VPC that SageMaker Studio is connected to.
Configure a new VPC for the Amazon Bedrock usage. Register the VPCs as peers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock interface VPC endpoints, powered by AWS PrivateLink, provide a private connection from a VPC to the Amazon Bedrock API and runtime endpoints. With private DNS enabled, Amazon Bedrock API calls from the VPC route through that endpoint rather than through public internet connectivity. [Use interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to create a private connection between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has developed a generative text summarization model by using Amazon Bedrock. The company will use Amazon Bedrock automatic model evaluation capabilities.  
  
Which metric should the company use to evaluate the accuracy of the model?

options.text: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) score

questions.explanation:
BERTScore leverages contextual embeddings from pre-trained language models to evaluate semantic similarity between generated summaries and reference text. Unlike surface-level metrics like ROUGE, BERTScore captures deeper meaning and context, making it particularly effective for evaluating generative text summarization quality. It directly aligns with Amazon Bedrock's automatic model evaluation capabilities for text generation tasks. AUC is for classification, F1 score is for classification/retrieval balance, and RWK score is not a standard evaluation metric.

**Learn more:** [Use metrics to understand model performance - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-metrics.html)

questions.question: Which term describes the instructions provided to foundation models (FMs) so that the FMs give a more accurate answer to a question?
questions.explanation:
A prompt is the instruction or input given to a foundation model to guide the response it generates.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is a prompt? - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/what-is-a-prompt.html)

Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?

questions.question:

Which AWS solution meets this requirement?

\

questions.question:
A company wants to use an ML model to detect harmful language in the comments section of social-media posts. The company will not use labeled data to train the model.  
  
Which strategy should the company use to detect harmful language?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms to train the model.
Use Amazon Polly to monitor comments.

questions.explanation:

\
**Learn more:** [Amazon Comprehend Trust and safety](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/trust-safety.html)

questions.question: Which category of AI model is used to predict numeric values?
questions.explanation:

questions.question:
A company uses a pre-trained open-source model to analyze user sentiment for a recently released product.  
  
Which action is the company required to perform according to MLOps best practices?

options.text: Use deep learning to perform hyperparameter tuning.
Collect user reviews and label each review as positive or negative.
Perform feature engineering on the input dataset.

questions.explanation:
MLOps includes continuously monitoring a model’s production performance and behavior so that degradation, drift, staleness, and other output issues can be detected and addressed.\
\
**Learn more:** [MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/mlops-continuous-delivery-and-automation-pipelines-in-machine-learning)

questions.question:
A company uses a pre-trained open-source model to analyze user sentiment for a recently released product.  
  
Which action is the company required to perform according to MLOps best practices?

options.text: Reduce the size of the training dataset.
Ensure that the ML model predictions are consistent with historical results.
Create a different ML model for each demographic group.
Measure class imbalance on the training dataset. Adapt the training process accordingly.

questions.explanation:
To develop an unbiased ML model for loan allocations, it is critical to measure and address class imbalance in the training dataset and adapt the training process accordingly (e.g., through resampling or weighted loss functions). Class imbalance can cause models to favor majority classes, perpetuating bias. Reducing training data (A) is counterproductive; ensuring consistency with historical results (B) perpetuates past biases; creating separate models per demographic (C) is itself discriminatory.

**Learn more:** [SageMaker Clarify: class imbalance bias metric](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-bias-metric-class-imbalance.html) · [Pre-training data bias detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-detect-data-bias.html)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],What is the purpose of chunking in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?

options.text: To avoid database storage limitations for large text documents by storing parts or chunks of the text
To improve efficiency by avoiding the need to convert large text into vector embeddings
To improve the contextual relevancy of results retrieved from the vector index
To decrease the cost of storage by storing parts or chunks of the text

questions.explanation:
Chunking creates smaller, semantically focused passages that can be embedded and retrieved independently from a vector index. Retrieving only the passages most relevant to a query provides more focused context and improves result relevance.

**Learn more:** [Chunk and vectorize by document layout or structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-how-to-semantic-chunking) · [How to Use Fabric for Retrieval Augmented Generation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-science/quickstart-building-retrieval-augmented-generation)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial company uses AI systems to obtain customer credit scores as part of its loan application process. The company plans to expand into a new market in a different geographic area and must ensure it can operate there.  
  
Which compliance laws should the company review?

options.text: Local payment card data protection laws

questions.explanation:
Local algorithm accountability laws can regulate AI-driven credit-scoring and lending decisions, including requirements concerning transparency, bias assessment, automated-decision safeguards, and accountability. These laws are directly relevant when deploying an AI credit-scoring process in a new jurisdiction.

**Learn more:** [AWS Well-Architected Responsible AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/responsible-ai-lens/responsible-ai-lens.html) · [AWS Certified AI Practitioner Exam Guide – Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial services company needs to ensure that its generative AI-powered chatbot gives factual responses to meet regulatory-compliance requirements.  
  
Which solution prevents the underlying foundation model (FM) from hallucinating?

options.text: Use AWS Config to query compliance metadata by using natural language.
Configure Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to evaluate user inputs and model responses.
Use Amazon Fraud Detector to detect potentially fraudulent online activities.
Use AWS Audit Manager to prepare IT audit and compliance reports.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails evaluates user inputs and model responses. Its contextual grounding checks can detect and filter hallucinated responses that are ungrounded in a provided source or factually inaccurate, supporting factual-response controls for regulated applications.

**Learn more:** [Use contextual grounding check to filter hallucinations in responses](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-contextual-grounding-check.html) · [Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A social media company wants to use a large language model (LLM) for content moderation. The company wants to evaluate the LLM outputs for bias and potential discrimination against specific groups or individuals.  

Which data source should the company use to evaluate the LLM outputs with the LEAST administrative effort?
questions.explanation:
Benchmark datasets are pre-designed, curated collections specifically created for evaluating AI models on fairness, bias, and discrimination. Using established benchmarks requires the least administrative effort compared to alternatives: user-generated content requires manual labeling, moderation logs require subjective review, and content guidelines are inherently subjective. Benchmarks provide standardized, reproducible evaluation with minimal overhead.

**Learn more:** [Use prompt datasets for model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-prompt-datasets.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical company is customizing a foundation model (FM) for diagnostic purposes. The company needs the model to be transparent and explainable to meet regulatory requirements.  

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the security and compliance by using Amazon Inspector.
Generate simple metrics, reports, and examples by using Amazon SageMaker Clarify.
Encrypt and secure training data by using Amazon Macie.
Gather more data. Use Amazon Rekognition to add custom labels to the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify is purpose-built to make machine learning models transparent and explainable by generating metrics, reports, and feature importance analyses. It identifies potential bias in data and model predictions, which is critical for regulatory compliance in healthcare and other sensitive domains. Amazon Inspector performs security scanning, Macie detects sensitive data, and Rekognition is for image recognition—none provide explainability or bias measurement.

**Learn more:** [Evaluate, explain, and detect bias in models – Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-explainability.html) · [Amazon SageMaker Clarify – Bias Detection and Explainability](https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/ai/clarify/)

questions.question: Which AWS service provides foundation models (FMs) to help users build and scale generative AI applications?

questions.question:
An education company plans to build a private-tutor application. The application will allow users to enter text or submit an image of a question. It will return a written answer along with an explanation of that written answer.  
  
Which model type satisfies these requirements?

A multimodal LLM can interpret both textual and image inputs and generate a textual response, including an answer and its explanation. Microsoft Foundry documents vision-enabled chat models as large multimodal models that analyze images and provide text responses.\

questions.question:
A financial company wants to label all credit-card activity as either possibly fraudulent or non-fraudulent, based on transaction data.

questions.question:
A financial company wants to label all credit-card activity as either possibly fraudulent or non-fraudulent, based on transaction data.  
  
Which type of ML model satisfies these requirements?

options.text: The conversion rate of customers who purchase products after AI assistant interactions.
The number of customer interactions with the AI assistant
Sentiment analysis scores from customer feedback after AI assistant interactions

questions.explanation:
The conversion rate of customers who make purchases after interacting with the AI assistant measures the proportion of assistant-engaged customers who complete a sale, directly tying the assistant’s use to sales outcomes.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use a large language model (LLM) to generate concise, feature-specific descriptions for the company’s products.  
  
Which prompt engineering technique meets these requirements?

options.text: Create one prompt that covers all products. Edit the responses to make the responses more specific, concise, and tailored to each product.
Create prompts for each product category that highlight the key features. Include the desired output format and length for each prompt response.
Include a diverse range of product features in each prompt to generate creative and unique descriptions.
Provide detailed, product-specific prompts to ensure precise and customized descriptions.

questions.explanation:
Creating tailored prompts for each product category that highlight key features and specify desired output format and length provides a systematic, scalable approach to prompt engineering. This technique balances customization with efficiency, ensuring concise and feature-specific descriptions without excessive manual editing. Option A requires post-processing, C introduces noise with irrelevant features, and D scales poorly across a product catalog.

**Learn more:** [Prompt engineering concepts - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html) · [Design a prompt - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/design-a-prompt.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is using Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks to build and train ML models. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to manage the flow of data from Amazon S3 to SageMaker Studio notebooks.  

Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon Inspector to monitor SageMaker Studio.
Use Amazon Macie to monitor SageMaker Studio.
Configure SageMaker to use a VPC with an S3 endpoint.
Configure SageMaker to use S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

questions.explanation:
Configuring SageMaker to use a VPC with an S3 endpoint enables secure, private data transfer between SageMaker Studio notebooks and S3 buckets without routing traffic through the public internet. An S3 VPC endpoint (particularly a gateway endpoint) provides the necessary infrastructure to efficiently manage and govern data flow from S3 to the compute environment. Amazon Inspector and Macie are monitoring/security services, while S3 Glacier is for archival storage.

**Learn more:** [Connect to Amazon SageMaker Studio Through an Interface VPC Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/studio-interface-endpoint.html)

A company operates an application on servers in an Amazon VPC. The company’s application uses Amazon Bedrock APIs for AI capabilities. The company does not want API calls to traverse the public internet.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use AWS PrivateLink to establish a private connection between the Amazon VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
Sign API requests by using an access key ID and a secret access key that is associated with an IAM principal.
Move the application to an on-premises server. Make API calls to the public endpoint of Amazon Bedrock.
Encrypt the data in transit from clients to the APIs that have been implemented in the Amazon VPC. Encrypt the data in transit for API calls from the Amazon VPC to Amazon Bedrock.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon Bedrock interface VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between the VPC and Amazon Bedrock. Bedrock API traffic can use this endpoint without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or public IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Use interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to create a private connection between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
A company uses multiple ML models and needs to detect changes in the original quality of its models so it can resolve any issues.  
  
Which AWS service or feature satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors machine learning models in production, detects drift or deviations in model-quality metrics such as accuracy, and can alert operators so they can take corrective action.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html)

questions.question:

questions.explanation:
Generative pre-trained transformers (GPT) excel at natural language understanding and code generation tasks. A GPT model can be fine-tuned to translate natural language employee queries into structured SQL queries, making database access accessible to non-technical users. Residual neural networks are for image classification, support vector machines are for classification/regression, and WaveNet generates audio—none are suited for natural language to SQL translation.

questions.question:
An AI practitioner wants an LLM to generate outputs that are more diverse and more creative.  
  
How should the AI practitioner modify the inference parameter?
questions.explanation:
A higher temperature increases randomness in token selection by making lower-probability tokens more likely to be chosen, which produces more diverse and creative responses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html)

questions.question:
A financial services company keeps patterns of fraudulent activity in a database and uses the data to perform investigations.  
  
The company wants to use a graph-based ML solution to build an AI tool that supports these investigations.  
  
Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database service designed for highly connected data and fraud-detection use cases. Neptune ML applies graph neural networks to graph data to identify hidden relationships and patterns that can support fraud investigations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Amazon Neptune ML for machine learning on graphs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/machine-learning.html) · [What Is Amazon Neptune?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/intro.html)

questions.question:
A company must perform numerical transformations on a set of images to transpose and rotate them.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Create a deep neural network by using the images as input.
Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the transformations.
Use an Amazon Bedrock large language model (LLM) with a high temperature.
Use AWS Glue Data Quality to make corrections to each image.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda can run custom image-transformation code on demand, such as code that transposes and rotates images. It is serverless and automatically manages infrastructure and scaling, minimizing operational overhead for image-processing workloads.\
\
**Learn more:** [AWS Lambda Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-functions-chapter.html) · [Get started with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless/latest/devguide/starter-lambda.html)

options.text: Use Amazon Macie to scan the model's output for sensitive data and set up alerts for potential violations.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to monitor the model's responses and create alerts for any detected personal information.
Use Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock to filter content. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms for notification of policy violations.
Implement Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to detect data drift and receive alerts when model quality degrades.

questions.explanation:
Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock enforce content policies to filter sensitive information (such as PII) from model outputs before users receive responses. Combined with Amazon CloudWatch alarms configured to trigger on policy violations, this provides both preventive filtering and alerting. Amazon Macie scans data in S3, not model outputs; CloudTrail logs API calls but doesn't filter content; Model Monitor detects data drift, not privacy violations.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html) · [Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Alarms.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a large collection of web data to create a large language model (LLM). The company randomly initializes the model’s weights. Next, the company trains the model on the data using a language-objective modeling function.  
  
Which stage of the model-training process does this scenario represent?
questions.explanation:
Pre-training builds a foundation model from scratch by learning general language patterns from a very large, broad dataset. Randomly initialized weights trained with a language-modeling objective describe this initial training stage; fine-tuning instead adapts an existing pre-trained model to a narrower task or domain dataset.

questions.question:
An AI practitioner wants to predict the classification of flowers based on petal length, petal width, sepal length, and sepal width.  
  
Which algorithm meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
K-nearest neighbors (k-NN) is a supervised classification algorithm that predicts the class of a data point by finding the k closest labeled examples in the training set. This directly matches the requirement to classify flower species based on petal and sepal measurements. K-means is unsupervised clustering, ARIMA is for time-series forecasting, and linear regression is for continuous value prediction—none address the classification problem.\
\
**Learn more:** [K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) Algorithm - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/knn.html)

Sentiment analysis is an NLP capability that evaluates unstructured text and assigns sentiment such as positive, neutral, negative, or mixed. An LLM can process the feedback text and perform this classification directly. Regression, recommendation, and time-series algorithms are intended for different problem types.

**Learn more:** [How to: Use Sentiment analysis and Opinion Mining](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/language-service/sentiment-opinion-mining/how-to/call-api)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
A company keeps its AI datasets in Amazon S3 buckets. The company plans to share the S3 buckets with its business partners and must avoid accidentally exposing sensitive data.  
  
Which AWS service should the company use to discover sensitive data in the dataset?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Macie automates the discovery, logging, and reporting of sensitive data in Amazon S3. It can inspect S3 objects through automated sensitive data discovery or targeted discovery jobs, helping identify data that should not be shared.\
\
**Learn more:** [Discovering sensitive data with Macie](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/data-classification.html)

questions.question:
A manufacturing company operates an application that ingests consumer complaints from publicly available sources. The application relies on complex, hard-coded logic to process those complaints. The company wants to scale this logic across markets and product lines.  
  
Which advantage do generative AI models provide for this scenario?

options.text: Less sensitivity to changes in inputs

questions.explanation:
Generative AI foundation models can be adapted for specific tasks and domains using prompting, grounding, or fine-tuning. This flexibility lets complaint-processing behavior be extended across different markets and product lines without encoding every variation as rigid application logic.\
\
**Learn more:** [Develop a generative AI application](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/ai-ml/generative-ai/develop-generative-ai-application)

questions.question:
A company is developing an AI application to summarize books of different lengths. During testing, the application cannot summarize certain books.  
  
Why does the application fail to summarize certain books?

options.text: The temperature is set too high.
The selected model does not support fine-tuning.
The Top P value is too high.
The input tokens exceed the model’s context size.

questions.explanation:
A model can process only a fixed maximum number of tokens in its context window. A book whose input token count exceeds that limit cannot be fully submitted for summarization; the request may fail or require chunking/truncation. Temperature and Top P control sampling, while fine-tuning support does not determine the maximum input length.\
\
**Learn more:** [OpenAI API Reference — Responses streaming](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming/response/reasoning_summary_part/added?lang=node.js)

questions.question:
A hospital plans to use a generative AI solution with speech-to-text capabilities to help employees improve their skills in dictating clinical notes.  
  
Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
AWS HealthScribe combines speech recognition and generative AI to transcribe patient-clinician conversations and generate reviewable clinical notes, making it the AWS service designed for clinical documentation workflows.\
\
**Learn more:** [AWS HealthScribe](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/health-scribe.html)

questions.question:
A hospital plans to use a generative AI solution with speech-to-text capabilities to help employees improve their skills in dictating clinical notes.  
  
Which AWS service satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the model on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Deploy the model on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
Deploy the model by using Amazon CloudFront with an Amazon S3 integration.
Deploy the model by using an Amazon SageMaker endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker endpoints provide a fully managed, serverless inference service. The company can deploy its model without provisioning or managing servers—SageMaker automatically handles resource allocation, scaling, and maintenance. EC2 (A) and EKS (B) require infrastructure management, and CloudFront with S3 (C) is not suitable for ML model inference.

**Learn more:** [Real-time inference endpoints - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/realtime-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
An ecommerce company receives several gigabytes of customer data each day. The company uses this data to train an ML model that forecasts future product demand. The company requires a solution to run inferences once per day.  
  
Which type of inference satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Batch inference is suited to periodic processing of large accumulated datasets, such as daily demand-forecast predictions. Amazon SageMaker AI Batch Transform is specifically intended to obtain inferences from large datasets without maintaining a persistent endpoint.\
\
**Learn more:** [Batch transform for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-transform.html)

questions.question:
An ecommerce company receives several gigabytes of customer data each day. The company uses this data to train an ML model that forecasts future product demand. The company requires a solution to run inferences once per day.  
  
Which type of inference satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs) visualize the relationship between specific input features and model predictions, showing how changes in each feature affect the forecast. This provides transparency and explainability for non-technical stakeholders by demonstrating the model's decision logic. Training code, sample data, and convergence tables do not offer explainability insights.

**Learn more:** [Partial dependence plots - SageMaker Clarify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-partial-dependence-plots.html) · [Model explainability with SageMaker Clarify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-explainability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to fine-tune a foundation model (FM) for a particular use case. The company must deploy the FM on Amazon Bedrock for internal use.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Run responses that have been generated by a pre-trained FM through Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to create the custom FM.
Use Amazon Personalize to customize the FM with custom data.
Use conversational builder for Amazon Bedrock Agents to create the custom model.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI to customize the FM. Then, import the trained model into Amazon Bedrock.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker AI can customize a foundation model through training or fine-tuning. Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import supports importing foundation models customized in environments such as SageMaker AI, after which the imported model can be used for inference in Amazon Bedrock.

**Learn more:** [Use Custom model import to import a customized open-source model into Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-import-model.html) · [Submit a model import job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-import-model-job.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company keeps customer data in OpenSearch. The company needs an AI solution that retrieves specific customer information from the stored data. The AI solution must translate queries into data requests and create CSV files from the results. It must then upload the CSV files to Amazon S3.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient way?

options.text: Create an AI agent to perform the required steps.
Use a single foundation model (FM) with few-shot prompting.
Create a software application without using AI to perform the required steps.
Train a decision tree model to generate a solution based on user questions.

questions.explanation:
An AI agent can orchestrate a multi-step workflow through action groups: it interprets user input, selects and invokes defined API or function operations, and passes parameters to business logic such as querying OpenSearch, producing CSV files, and uploading those files to Amazon S3. This provides managed tool orchestration with less custom operational code than implementing the workflow directly. [How Amazon Bedrock Agents works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-how.html)

**Learn more:** [How Amazon Bedrock Agents works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-how.html) · [Use action groups to define actions for your agent to perform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-action-create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An accounting firm wants to implement a large language model (LLM) to automate document processing. The firm must proceed responsibly to avoid potential harms.  

What should the firm do when developing and deploying the LLM? (Choose two.)

options.text: Include fairness metrics for model evaluation.
Adjust the temperature parameter of the model.
Modify the training data to mitigate bias.
Avoid overfitting on the training data.

questions.explanation:
Responsible AI development for document automation requires two complementary practices: including fairness metrics ensures the model doesn't discriminate against groups or introduce harmful bias in processing outcomes; modifying training data to mitigate bias addresses the root cause by ensuring the model learns from representative, balanced examples. Temperature adjustment affects output randomness, not ethics; overfitting prevention and prompt engineering are optimization techniques but don't directly address responsible development principles.

**Learn more:** [Fairness and bias detection with SageMaker Clarify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-configure-processing-jobs.html) · [Pre-training Data Bias](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-detect-data-bias.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An AI practitioner has built a deep learning model to classify the types of materials in images. The AI practitioner now wants to measure the model performance.  
  
Which metric will help the AI practitioner evaluate the performance of the model?
questions.explanation:
A confusion matrix is the standard evaluation metric for classification models, providing counts of true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives that enable calculation of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. R2 and MSE are regression metrics; correlation matrices describe feature relationships but don't evaluate model performance on a specific classification task.

**Learn more:** [Use advanced metrics in your analyses – Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-advanced-metrics.html) · [Model Quality Metrics – Amazon SageMaker](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-model-quality-metrics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company monitors a predictive model by using Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor. The company detects data drift that exceeds a defined threshold and wants to mitigate a potentially negative effect on the predictive model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Re-train the model with fresh data.

questions.explanation:
Data drift can cause a model to lose predictive accuracy because the production data distribution differs from the data on which it was trained. Retraining the model with fresh, representative data adapts it to that changed distribution and mitigates the adverse impact.

**Learn more:** [Data and model quality monitoring with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html) · [Data quality - Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-data-quality.html)

questions.question:
A company needs to build and deploy ML models on AWS without writing any code.  
  
Which AWS service or feature satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Canvas provides a visual no-code interface to prepare data, build and train machine learning models, and deploy them for production predictions without writing code.\
\
**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker Canvas](https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/ai/canvas/) · [Amazon SageMaker Canvas documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question: Which statement identifies an advantage of using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for natural language processing (NLP) tasks?

options.text: RAG can use external knowledge sources to generate more accurate and informative responses.
RAG is designed to improve the speed of language model training.
RAG is primarily used for speech recognition tasks.
RAG is a technique for data augmentation in computer vision tasks.

questions.explanation:
Retrieval Augmented Generation grounds a language model’s output in retrieved external data, allowing it to incorporate relevant information beyond its training data and produce more accurate, informative, and contextually relevant responses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and indexes in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/retrieval-augmented-generation?view=foundry-classic)

questions.question:
A real estate company is building an ML model that uses sales and marketing data to predict house prices. The company wants to apply feature engineering to create a model that produces accurate predictions.  
  
Which approach meets these requirements?

options.text: Understand patterns by providing data visualization.
Create or select relevant features for model training.

questions.explanation:
Feature engineering involves creating and selecting relevant input variables for model training so that the model receives predictive information. Relevant features derived from sales and marketing data can improve house-price prediction accuracy.\
\
**Learn more:** [Feature engineering - AWS Well-Architected Machine Learning Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/feature-engineering.html)

questions.question:
A company uses AI to create a toy-recommendation website that recommends toys according to a customer’s interests and age. The company observes that the AI often recommends stereotypically gendered toys.  
  
Which AWS service or feature should the company use to examine this bias?
questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects and measures potential bias in training data and model predictions, enabling fairness analysis across attributes such as gender and age.\
\
**Learn more:** [Fairness, model explainability and bias detection with SageMaker Clarify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-configure-processing-jobs.html) · [Generate Reports for Bias in Pre-training Data in SageMaker Studio](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-data-bias-reports-ui.html)

questions.question:
An AI practitioner must improve the accuracy of a natural language generation model. The model relies on rapidly changing inventory data.  
  
Which technique will improve the model’s accuracy?
questions.explanation:
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant, current inventory data from an external knowledge source and adds it to the model context before generation. This grounds responses in up-to-date information instead of relying only on the model’s static training knowledge.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understanding Retrieval Augmented Generation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/retrieval-augmented-generation-options/what-is-rag.html) · [Retrieval Augmented Generation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-foundation-models-customize-rag.html)

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant content from authoritative company data sources and includes that content in the LLM’s generation context. This produces responses grounded in current, domain-specific facts and can support source traceability and accuracy checking.

**Learn more:** [Retrieve data and generate AI responses with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html) · [Understanding Retrieval Augmented Generation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/retrieval-augmented-generation-options/what-is-rag.html)

questions.question:
A healthcare company wants to develop a model that improves disease diagnostics by analyzing patient voices. The company has recorded hundreds of patient voices for this project.  
  
The company is currently filtering voice recordings based on duration and language.  
  
Which ML lifecycle phase describes the project’s current stage?
questions.explanation:
Data preprocessing prepares collected raw data for modeling by cleaning, filtering, validating, and selecting appropriate records. Filtering voice recordings by duration and language is a preprocessing activity.\
\
**Learn more:** [ML lifecycle: data processing (AWS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/ml-lifecycle-phase-data-processing.html) · [Data preprocessing (AWS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/data-preprocessing.html)

questions.question:
A healthcare company wants to develop a model that improves disease diagnostics by analyzing patient voices. The company has recorded hundreds of patient voices for this project.  
  
The company is currently filtering voice recordings based on duration and language.  
  
Which ML lifecycle phase describes the project’s current stage?

options.text: Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Fraud Detector to build the application.
Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases to build the application.
Use Amazon Personalize with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases to build the application.
Use Amazon SageMaker to build the application by training a new ML model.

questions.explanation:
Agents for Amazon Bedrock combined with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases provides the infrastructure to build conversational AI applications that can search, retrieve, and present claim information and documents. Agents handle natural language interaction with users, while knowledge bases store and retrieve claim data efficiently. Amazon Fraud Detector is for fraud detection, Amazon Personalize is for recommendations, and building a custom model with SageMaker is unnecessary and inefficient for this use case.

**Learn more:** [Automate tasks in your application using AI agents - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html) · [Augment response generation for your agent with a knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-kb-add.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to build an ML model that detects abnormal patterns in sensor data. The company has no labeled training data.  
  
Which ML method meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Autoencoders support unsupervised anomaly detection by learning to reconstruct the prevalent normal sensor-data patterns. Observations that produce high reconstruction error can be treated as abnormal, so labeled anomaly examples are not required. Unsupervised methods are appropriate for anomaly-detection tasks involving unlabeled data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Unsupervised Built-in SageMaker AI Algorithms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/algorithms-unsupervised.html) · [Types of Algorithms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/algorithms-choose.html)

questions.question:
A company has policies for storing and deleting data.  
  
Which data-governance strategy is being described?
questions.explanation:
Data retention establishes requirements for how long data must be kept and when it must be deleted or disposed of.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data retention (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/data-retention.html)

questions.question:
A company built a deep learning model for object detection and deployed the model to production.  

Which AI process occurs when the model analyzes a new image to identify objects?
questions.explanation:
Inference is the process of using a trained model to make predictions on new, unseen data. When the deployed model analyzes a new image to identify objects, it is performing inference—applying learned patterns to generate predictions. Training builds the model; deployment puts it in production; bias correction adjusts model fairness after deployment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Deploy models for inference (SageMaker AI)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model.html)

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes embeddings in generative AI?

options.text: Embeddings represent data as high-dimensional vectors that capture semantic relationships.
Embeddings is a technique that searches data to find the most helpful information to answer natural language questions.
Embeddings reduce the hardware requirements of a model by using a less precise data type for the weights and activations.
Embeddings provide the ability to store and retrieve data for generative AI applications.

questions.explanation:
Embeddings represent data as high-dimensional numerical vectors that capture semantic relationships, allowing related concepts or content to be close together in vector space.\
\
**Learn more:** [Amazon Titan Text Embeddings models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/titan-embedding-models.html)

questions.question:
A company is developing a job-recommendation system using job-posting data and job-seeker user profiles. The system displays gender-based bias in job recommendations for user profiles that are otherwise equivalent.  
  
Which AWS responsible-AI best-practice principle should the company follow to resolve this issue?
questions.explanation:
Fairness addresses an AI system’s impact on different groups of stakeholders and requires detecting and mitigating biased outcomes, including gender-based differences for otherwise equivalent users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Responsible AI - Generative AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/responsible-ai.html)

options.text: Using a third-party enterprise application that has embedded generative AI features.
Building an application by using an existing third-party generative AI foundation model (FM).
Refining an existing third-party generative AI foundation model (FM) by fine-tuning the model by using data specific to the business.
Building and training a generative AI model from scratch by using specific data that a customer owns.

questions.explanation: Building and training a generative AI model from scratch gives the company responsibility for securing the full model-development scope, including the customer-owned data and the training process. Higher-level consumption, application-building, and fine-tuning scopes leave more of the underlying model responsibilities with a third-party provider.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to fine-tune a foundation model (FM) by using AWS services. The company must ensure that its data remains private, safe, and secure in the source AWS Region where the data is stored.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way? (Choose two.)

options.text: Host the model on premises by using AWS Outposts.
Use AWS PrivateLink and a VPC.
Host the Amazon Bedrock API on premises.
Use Amazon CloudWatch logs and metrics.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock provides managed foundation-model fine-tuning, eliminating the cost and operational overhead of hosting model infrastructure. Configuring a VPC with AWS PrivateLink protects model-customization data and jobs by using private connectivity to Amazon Bedrock rather than public internet access.

**Learn more:** [Customize a model with fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-fine-tuning.html) · [Protect your data using Amazon VPC and AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/usingVPC.html)

questions.question:
An AI practitioner is using a large language model (LLM) to create content for marketing campaigns. The generated content sounds plausible and factual but is incorrect.  

Which problem is the LLM having?
questions.explanation:
Hallucination in LLMs refers to the generation of plausible-sounding but factually incorrect content. The model produces coherent text that appears authoritative but lacks grounding in actual facts or training data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Minimize generative AI hallucinations with Amazon Bedrock Automated Reasoning checks](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/minimize-generative-ai-hallucinations-with-amazon-bedrock-automated-reasoning-checks/)

questions.question:
A company uses an Amazon Nova Canvas model to generate images, and the model generates the images successfully.  
  
The company must prevent the model from including particular items in the generated images.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Nova Canvas uses a negative prompt (`negativeText`) to specify objects or characteristics that should be excluded from an image. AWS documents negative prompts specifically for steering generation away from undesired elements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Negative prompts - Amazon Nova](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/prompting-image-negative.html) · [Request and response structure for image generation - Amazon Nova](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/image-gen-req-resp-structure.html)

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
questions.question:
A company needs to deploy a secure AI system with controlled access. The system must permit only authorized personnel to access model training data.  
  
Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) securely controls access to AWS resources by using policies attached to users, groups, and roles. IAM permissions can limit model-training-data access to authorized personnel only.\
\
**Learn more:** [Access management for AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access.html)

questions.question: What benefit does a company obtain by using ongoing pre-training to fine-tune a foundation model (FM)?

options.text: Decreased time required to train the model

questions.explanation:
Ongoing or continued pre-training updates a foundation model with additional data over time, extending its knowledge and improving its performance, particularly for relevant domains or evolving information.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data lifecycle in generative AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/strategy-data-considerations-gen-ai/lifecycle.html) · [Choosing an AWS generative AI service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/generative-ai-on-aws-how-to-choose/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a product-recommendation application using a generative AI model. The company needs to minimize the environmental impact of the application.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Optimize the deployed model architecture to prioritize computational efficiency during model inference.
Adopt a distributed inference approach by using multiple smaller models across multiple Availability Zones.
Adopt a hybrid strategy by deploying the model on premises and storing the data on AWS.
Deploy multiple models and use a dynamic model selection mechanism that queries different models randomly.

questions.explanation:
Optimizing the deployed model architecture for computationally efficient inference reduces the compute and energy required for each prediction, thereby reducing the application’s environmental impact. AWS sustainability guidance for generative AI recommends smaller models and optimized inference techniques to reduce carbon footprint.

**Learn more:** [Sustainability – AWS Well-Architected Generative AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/sustainability.html) · [Guidance for Optimizing Deep Learning Workloads for Sustainability on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/optimizing-deep-learning-workloads-for-sustainability-on-aws/)

questions.question:
A company wants to use large language models (LLMs) to produce code from natural language code comments.  
  
Which LLM feature meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Text completion is the LLM capability that takes a partial input — such as a natural-language code comment — and predicts the most probable continuation, which is exactly the mechanism code assistants use to turn a comment into working code. Text generation is the broader, open-ended content-creation capability, while text summarization and text classification describe condensing or labeling existing text rather than continuing a prompt with new code.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is a large language model (LLM)?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/large-language-model/)

questions.question:
A company wants to use large language models (LLMs) to produce code from natural language code comments.  
  
Which LLM feature meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a binary classification model to generate code reviews.
Install code recommendation software in the company's developer tools.
Install a code forecasting tool to predict potential code issues.
Use a natural language processing (NLP) tool to generate code.

questions.explanation:
Installing an AI-powered code recommendation tool (such as Amazon Q Developer) directly in the company's IDEs gives developers real-time, context-aware code suggestions inside their existing workflow, which is the most direct, low-friction way to raise coding productivity across a development team. A binary classifier is not suited to generating code reviews, a code-forecasting tool only flags potential issues rather than speeding up writing code, and a generic NLP code-generation tool is a vaguer, less workflow-integrated solution than an IDE-embedded recommendation assistant.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Q Developer](https://aws.amazon.com/q/developer/) · [Use Amazon Q Developer as a coding assistant to increase your productivity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/use-q-developer-as-coding-assistant-to-increase-productivity.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to keep its foundation model (FM) relevant by using the latest data. The company wants to implement a model-training strategy that includes regular updates to the FM.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Continuous pre-training extends a foundation model’s pre-training phase by training it on additional data, allowing the model to acquire new knowledge from newly available corpora and remain current through regular updates.\
\
**Learn more:** [Continued pre-training (CPT) – Amazon Nova](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-cpt.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to keep its foundation model (FM) relevant by using the latest data. The company wants to implement a model-training strategy that includes regular updates to the FM.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Nova Micro uses transformer-based architectures. Nova Lite does not use transformer-based architectures.
Nova Micro supports only text data. Nova Lite is optimized for numerical data.
Nova Micro supports only text. Nova Lite supports images, videos, and text.
Nova Micro runs only on CPUs. Nova Lite runs only on GPUs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Nova Micro accepts text input only, whereas Amazon Nova Lite is a low-cost multimodal model that accepts text, image, and video inputs. Nova Lite therefore supports the image-based and document-processing workload; Micro does not directly accept images.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Nova?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/what-is-nova.html) · [Nova Lite model card](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-amazon-nova-lite.html)

questions.question:
A company wants to create a new solution by using AWS Glue. The company has minimal programming experience with AWS Glue.  
  
Which AWS service can help the company use AWS Glue?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Q Developer is an AI-powered assistant that helps developers work with AWS services through natural language guidance and code examples. For users with minimal AWS Glue programming experience, Q Developer simplifies the process by providing step-by-step assistance, code generation, and explanations, reducing the learning curve. AWS Config (B) manages compliance, Personalize (C) handles recommendations, and Comprehend (D) performs NLP analysis.\
\

questions.question:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A loan company is building a generative AI-based solution to offer new applicants discounts based on specific business criteria. The company wants to build and use an AI model responsibly to minimize bias that could negatively affect some customers.  

Which actions should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Detect imbalances or disparities in the data.
Ensure that the model runs frequently.
Evaluate the model's behavior so that the company can provide transparency to stakeholders.
Use the Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) technique to ensure that the model is 100% accurate.
Ensure that the model's inference time is within the accepted limits.

questions.explanation:
Responsible AI for fair lending requires detecting data imbalances and disparities that could lead to discriminatory outcomes, and evaluating model behavior to provide transparency to stakeholders and regulators. Option A (data bias detection) addresses the root cause, while Option C (behavioral evaluation) ensures accountability and compliance. Options B (frequency), D (ROUGE scoring for classification tasks), and E (inference timing) don't address fairness concerns.

**Learn more:** [Pre-training Bias Metrics – Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-measure-data-bias.html) · [Evaluate, explain, and detect bias in models – Amazon SageMaker AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-explainability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a third-party model in Amazon Bedrock to analyze confidential documents. The company has concerns about data privacy.  
  
Which statement explains how Amazon Bedrock safeguards data privacy?

options.text: User inputs and model outputs are anonymized and shared with third-party model providers.
User inputs and model outputs are not shared with any third-party model providers.
User inputs are kept confidential, but model outputs are shared with third-party model providers.
User inputs and model outputs are redacted before the inputs and outputs are shared with third-party model providers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock deploys third-party models in AWS-managed model deployment accounts to which the model providers have no access. Consequently, model providers cannot access Amazon Bedrock logs, customer prompts, or model completions; inputs and outputs are not shared with them unless a customer explicitly opts in to a model-specific data-sharing arrangement.

**Learn more:** [Data protection - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/data-protection.html) · [Amazon Bedrock abuse detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/abuse-detection.html)

Which metric meets this requirement?

ROUGE is a standard text-generation evaluation metric for summarization. It compares a generated summary with a reference summary using overlap-based measures, such as n-grams and longest common subsequences, to quantify summary quality.\

Fine-tune the LLM on the company policy data.
Implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for in-context responses.
Use pre-training and data augmentation on the company policy data.

questions.explanation:
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is the most cost-effective solution because it dynamically retrieves relevant policy information at inference time without requiring model retraining, fine-tuning, or pre-training. This approach avoids expensive computational overhead while enabling contextually accurate responses grounded in the company's policies. Full retraining (A), fine-tuning (B), and pre-training with augmentation (D) all require significant computational resources.

options.text: Remove personally identifiable information (PII) from the customer data before fine-tuning the LLM.
Increase the Top-K parameter of the LLM.
Store customer data in Amazon S3. Encrypt the data before fine-tuning the LLM.

questions.explanation:
Removing personally identifiable information (PII) from the fine-tuning dataset prevents the model from learning or memorizing identifiable customer details that could later be reproduced. Encryption protects data at rest, and Top-K changes output sampling behavior; neither prevents private data from being embedded in the trained model. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can block or mask sensitive information during inference, but data sanitization is the direct control for preventing PII exposure through the fine-tuned model.

**Learn more:** [Remove PII from conversations by using sensitive information filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-sensitive-filters.html)

Which type of bias is affecting the model output?
questions.explanation:
Sampling bias occurs when training data is not representative of the population, leading to poor performance on underrepresented groups. The disproportionate flagging of one ethnic group indicates the training dataset likely lacked balanced representation across demographics.\
\
**Learn more:** [Pre-training Data Bias (sampling bias) - SageMaker Clarify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-detect-data-bias.html)

Physically storing models for archival purposes.
