A company wants to develop an educational game where users answer questions such as the following: "A jar contains six red, four green, and three yellow marbles. What is the probability of choosing a green marble from the jar?"  

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use supervised learning to create a regression model that will predict probability.
Use reinforcement learning to train a model to return the probability.
Use code that will calculate probability by using simple rules and computations.
Use unsupervised learning to create a model that will estimate probability density.

questions.explanation:
Probability questions with deterministic mathematical solutions (green marbles / total marbles) require no machine learning. Simple, straightforward code using basic arithmetic provides the lowest operational overhead and highest accuracy. Supervised regression, reinforcement learning, and unsupervised density estimation all introduce unnecessary complexity and resource consumption for a trivial calculation.

**Learn more:** [MLCOST02-BP01: Identify if machine learning is the right solution](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/mlcost02-bp01.html)

questions.question:
A company is building an ML model to predict the risk of heart disease. The model uses patient data such as age, cholesterol, blood pressure, smoking status, and exercise habits. The dataset contains a target value showing whether a patient has heart disease.  
  
Which ML technique meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Supervised learning trains on input features paired with known target labels. Here, the patient characteristics are the features and the heart-disease indicator is the label to be predicted, making this a classification task.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Machine Learning?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/machine-learning/) · [Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning](https://aws.amazon.com/compare/the-difference-between-machine-learning-supervised-and-unsupervised/)

questions.question:
A company is building an ML model to predict the risk of heart disease. The model uses patient data such as age, cholesterol, blood pressure, smoking status, and exercise habits. The dataset contains a target value showing whether a patient has heart disease.  
  
Which ML technique meets these requirements?

options.text: Deep learning model built on principal components

questions.explanation:
Logistic regression models provide transparent, interpretable weights for each input feature that directly influence predictions. Employees can easily view and manually adjust these weights based on their domain expertise and business knowledge to fine-tune lead prioritization. Deep learning models, neural networks, and k-NN lack this interpretability and are not amenable to manual weight adjustment by non-technical users.

**Learn more:** [What is Logistic Regression? - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/logistic-regression/)

questions.question:
A company needs to build an AI solution that automatically extracts structured and unstructured data from scanned PDF documents and forms.  
  
Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Textract uses OCR and document analysis to extract text and structured data, including form fields and tables, from scanned documents and PDFs.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Textract?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/what-is.html) · [Amazon Textract](https://aws.amazon.com/textract/)

questions.question:
A financial company uses ML to support some of its tasks.  
  
Which option represents a use of generative AI models?

options.text: Classifying customers based on product usage
Segmenting customers based on type of investments

questions.explanation:
Generative AI can produce new text, including concise summaries of existing customer complaints. Customer classification and segmentation assign records to groups, while revenue forecasting predicts a numerical future outcome.\
\
**Learn more:** [Generative AI use cases and resources (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/ai/generative-ai/use-cases/) · [Generative AI-powered case summarization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/use-generative-ai-case-summarization.html)

questions.question:
A financial company uses ML to support some of its tasks.  
  
Which option represents a use of generative AI models?

options.text: Generation of custom foundation models (FMs) to predict customer needs
Automation of repetitive tasks and orchestration of complex workflows
Automatically calling multiple foundation models (FMs) and consolidating the results
Selecting the foundation model (FM) based on predefined criteria and metrics

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Agents automate repetitive workflows and orchestrate complex, multi-step tasks across systems and data sources. For high-volume customer support, they streamline handling of routine inquiries while maintaining flexibility for varied questions.

**Learn more:** [Automate tasks using AI agents (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html) · [How Amazon Bedrock Agents works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-how.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An AI practitioner wants to use a foundation model (FM) to design a search application. The search application must handle queries that have text and images.  

Which type of FM should the AI practitioner use to power the search application?
questions.explanation:
Multi-modal embedding models are specifically designed to process and embed both text and image data into a shared vector space, enabling efficient semantic search across both modalities. Text embedding models handle only text, multi-modal generation models create outputs rather than search, and image generation models only generate images.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings G1](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-amazon-titan-multimodal-embeddings-g1.html) · [Overview of Amazon Titan models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/titan-models.html)

questions.question:
An AI practitioner has a database of animal photos. The AI practitioner wants to automatically identify and categorize the animals in the photos without manual human effort.  

Which strategy meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Object detection is a computer vision technique that automatically identifies, locates, and categorizes objects (in this case, animals) within images without manual intervention. It directly addresses the requirement to automatically identify and categorize animals at scale. Anomaly detection identifies outliers, named entity recognition works on text (not images), and inpainting fills missing image regions—none accomplish photo-based animal categorization.\
\
**Learn more:** [Detecting objects and concepts – Amazon Rekognition](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/labels.html)

questions.question:
A company is building a chatbot to improve user experience. The company is using a large language model (LLM) from Amazon Bedrock for intent detection. The company wants to use few-shot learning to improve intent detection accuracy.  

Which additional data does the company need to meet these requirements?

options.text: Pairs of chatbot responses and correct user intents
Pairs of user messages and correct chatbot responses
Pairs of user messages and correct user intents
Pairs of user intents and correct chatbot responses

questions.explanation:
Few-shot learning improves intent detection by providing the model with labeled examples mapping user messages to their correct intents. The model uses these input-output pairs to learn how to classify new user intents more accurately.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prompt engineering concepts (Amazon Bedrock)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html)

questions.question:
A company is building a chatbot to improve user experience. The company is using a large language model (LLM) from Amazon Bedrock for intent detection. The company wants to use few-shot learning to improve intent detection accuracy.  

Which additional data does the company need to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use the AI solution to make final hiring decisions without human review.
Train the AI solution exclusively on data from previous successful hires.
Test the AI solution to ensure that it does not discriminate against any protected groups.
Keep the AI decision-making process confidential to maintain a competitive advantage.

questions.explanation:
Responsible AI requires fairness assessment and bias mitigation across affected demographic groups. Testing the system for discriminatory outcomes against protected groups helps identify and prevent unfair hiring outcomes.

**Learn more:** [Mitigate unwanted bias directly in core AI system design — AWS Responsible AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/responsible-ai-lens/raisp02-bp03.html) · [Responsible AI — AWS Generative AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/responsible-ai.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon Bedrock to implement a generative AI solution that gives customers personalized product recommendations.  
  
The company needs to evaluate the AI solution’s impact on sales revenue.  
  
Which metric meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Conversion rate measures the percentage of customers who complete a purchase after receiving a recommendation, making it an appropriate metric for assessing the solution’s effect on revenue. AWS guidance recommends measuring conversion rates with appropriate attribution to determine whether realized revenue is directly contributed by a product change.

**Learn more:** [AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Developing product strategies that deliver measurable business value](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/prescriptive-guidance/latest/strategy-product-development/strategy-product-development.pdf?did=pg_card-pdf&trk=pg_card-pdf)

questions.question:
A company needs to gather a large dataset to train an AI assistant for a particular content area.  
  
Which dataset meets this requirement?

options.text: Diverse conversations that use relevant terminology
Time series data of general purpose historical sales
Unique product IDs and corresponding user IDs

questions.explanation:
Training a domain-specific AI assistant requires diverse natural-language conversations that contain terminology relevant to the target content area. This data helps the model learn the domain’s language, context, and likely user interactions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Domain 2: Fundamentals of Generative AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain2.html)

questions.question:
A hospital has developed an AI system that delivers personalized treatment recommendations for patients. The AI system must explain the reasoning behind its recommendations and make its insights accessible to doctors and patients.  
  
Which human-centered design principle is illustrated by this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Explainability requires an AI system’s recommendations and reasoning to be understandable and accessible to the people who use or are affected by it, including clinicians and patients.\
\
**Learn more:** [Responsible AI – Building AI Responsibly (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/ai/responsible-ai/) · [AWS Certified AI Practitioner Exam Guide – Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html)

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature stores embeddings in a vector database for use with foundation models (FMs) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
questions.explanation:
Amazon OpenSearch Service provides vector search, including vector fields for storing dense embeddings and similarity search. This supports RAG by retrieving semantically relevant context for foundation-model responses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Vector search - Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/vector-search.html)

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature stores embeddings in a vector database for use with foundation models (FMs) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
questions.explanation:
Continued pre-training extends a foundation model’s pre-training with additional unlabeled text from a particular domain, allowing it to learn domain-specific knowledge and terminology. Supervised fine-tuning instead requires labeled input-output pairs, while retrieval-augmented generation is not a fine-tuning method.

**Learn more:** [Continued pre-training (CPT) - Amazon Nova](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-cpt.html) · [Customize your model to improve its performance for your use case - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-models.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company trains image- and text-generation models on Amazon SageMaker AI. The company releases the models using Amazon Bedrock. The company must keep a tamper-proof, queryable record of every API call from SageMaker AI, Amazon Bedrock, and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).  
  
Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail Lake stores CloudTrail events in immutable event data stores and supports SQL-based queries. CloudTrail captures AWS API activity, enabling an auditable, tamper-resistant record of management API calls across services such as Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Bedrock, and IAM.

**Learn more:** [Working with AWS CloudTrail Lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.html) · [CloudTrail Lake concepts and terminology](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake-concepts.html)

questions.question:
A company uses Amazon Comprehend to analyze customer feedback. A customer has multiple uniquely trained models, and the company assigns an endpoint to each model by using Comprehend. The company wants to automate a report for every endpoint that has not been used for more than 15 days.  
  
Which service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
AWS Trusted Advisor includes an Amazon Comprehend underutilized-endpoints cost-optimization check. It flags endpoints that have not been actively used for real-time inference requests for more than 15 days, and its results refresh automatically each day.\

**Learn more:** [Using Trusted Advisor with Amazon Comprehend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/manage-endpoints-trusted-advisor.html)

Which AWS solution meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Average call duration is the most direct metric for measuring whether the chatbot reduces employee workload. Shorter calls indicate the chatbot is effectively assisting or resolving customer inquiries more quickly, directly reflecting the business objective of reducing employee actions. Website engagement rate, CSR initiatives, and regulatory compliance are not aligned with the stated goal of reducing call center work.

questions.question:
A company employs an Amazon Bedrock large language model (LLM) in an application. During testing, the company notices different outputs for the same input.  
  
What is the MOST likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The LLM is acting in a nondeterministic way.
The guardrails of the LLM are not configured properly.
The LLM is acting in a deterministic way.

questions.explanation:
LLMs can behave nondeterministically because they sample from probability distributions when generating tokens. Amazon Bedrock inference settings such as temperature and top-p control that randomness; higher randomness can produce different responses for the identical prompt.\
\
**Learn more:** [Influence response generation with inference parameters - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html)

questions.question:
A company employs an Amazon Bedrock large language model (LLM) in an application. During testing, the company notices different outputs for the same input.  
  
What is the MOST likely cause of this issue?

options.text: Use traditional ML algorithms with custom features extracted from the dataset.
Use a pre-trained deep learning model. Fine-tune the model on the dataset.
Use a generative adversarial network (GAN) model to classify the images.
Use a support vector machine (SVM) with manually engineered features for classification.

questions.explanation:
Traditional machine-learning algorithms can directly use the extracted custom features for classification, avoiding the additional work of selecting, adapting, and fine-tuning a deep-learning model. A GAN is primarily intended for generative tasks, while manually engineering features for an SVM is unnecessary when suitable custom features have already been extracted.

**Learn more:** [Difference between ML and deep learning (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/compare/the-difference-between-machine-learning-and-deep-learning/) · [What is deep learning? (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/deep-learning/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has built a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-based AI assistant using Amazon Bedrock Agents. At times, the AI assistant produces incomplete or inaccurate answers. The company wants to enhance and assess the AI assistant's performance.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use automated metrics such as Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) scores to measure response similarity to reference answers.
Monitor response latency and token generation speed to optimize performance.
Evaluate only the final answer quality against ground truth responses.
Confirm that the retrieved documents are relevant and that the final answers are accurate.

questions.explanation:
RAG quality depends on both retrieving context that is relevant to the request and generating an accurate answer grounded in that context. Amazon Bedrock RAG evaluations provide retrieval metrics such as context relevance and response metrics such as correctness, completeness, and faithfulness, allowing faults in either stage to be identified and improved.

**Learn more:** [Use metrics to understand RAG system performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-eval-retrieve.html) · [Evaluate the performance of RAG sources using Amazon Bedrock evaluations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/evaluation-kb.html)

questions.question:

Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference to deploy the model.
Use Amazon CloudFront to deploy the model.
Use Amazon API Gateway to host the model and serve predictions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference provides fully managed, infrastructure-agnostic model deployment with automatic scaling based on request volume—eliminating the need to provision or manage EC2 instances or other compute resources. CloudFront is a CDN; API Gateway routes traffic; AWS Batch processes batch workloads—none eliminate infrastructure management.

A global logistics company uses generative AI (GenAI) models on Amazon Bedrock to automate paperwork and shipment documentation. The company wants to establish a clear AI governance process to ensure that the models are used responsibly and comply with company policies.  
  
Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Set up a regular review process to check that the models' results are accurate and fair and follow company policies.
Provide training for all employees who work with AI tools so the employees understand company rules, data handling, and responsible AI use.
Let the cloud provider manage all AI safety checks and reviews to save internal effort.
Involve only developers in governance reviews because the developers build and deploy the AI systems.
Review the models only when users report problems or errors in the system.

questions.explanation:
Effective AI governance requires continuous, human-led review of model behavior for reliability, fairness, and conformance with organizational policies. It also requires that employees using AI understand applicable policies, proper data handling, and responsible-use practices. AWS responsible-AI guidance calls for regular review processes, governance involving technical, business, and risk-management perspectives, and human oversight of monitored systems.

questions.question:
A company wants to assess the costs that are associated with using a large language model (LLM) to generate inferences. The company wants to use Amazon Bedrock to build generative AI applications.  

Which factor will drive the inference costs?

options.text: Amount of data used to train the LLM

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock inference costs are driven by the number of tokens consumed (both input and output). Temperature, training data volume, and training time do not directly affect inference costs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Amazon Bedrock pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/)

questions.question:
A company needs to identify customer groups using customers’ demographics and purchasing patterns.  
  
Which algorithm should the company use to satisfy this requirement?
questions.explanation:
K-means is an unsupervised clustering algorithm that forms discrete groups of similar observations from their attributes, making it suitable for customer segmentation by demographics and purchasing behavior. questions.question:
A company plans to use large language models (LLMs) to build a chatbot. The chatbot will help customers with product inquiries, order tracking, and returns. It must be able to process text and image inputs to generate responses.  
  
Which AWS service fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation:

\
**Learn more:** [Amazon Bedrock User Guide — Supported foundation models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-supported.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to build a chatbot that answers employee questions about company policies. The policies are updated often, and the chatbot must reflect those changes in near real time. The company wants to select a large language model (LLM).  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Fine-tune an LLM on the company policy text by using Amazon SageMaker.
Select a foundation model (FM) from Amazon Bedrock to build an application.
Create a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow by using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
Use Amazon Q Business to build a custom Q App.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides a managed Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow that retrieves relevant proprietary policy content when a user asks a question. Its data sources can be synchronized incrementally so added, modified, and deleted policy documents are re-indexed without retraining or fine-tuning the LLM.

**Learn more:** [Retrieve data and generate AI responses with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html) · [Sync your data with your Amazon Bedrock knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-data-source-sync-ingest.html)

questions.question:
An airline company plans to use a generative AI model to convert a flight-booking system from one programming language to another. The company must choose a model for this task.  
  
Which criteria should the company use to select the appropriate generative AI model for this task?

options.text: Syntax, semantic understanding, and code optimization capabilities
Code generation speed and error handling capabilities

questions.explanation:
Programming-language conversion depends on correctly understanding source-code syntax and semantics and generating equivalent, optimized code in the target language.\
\
**Learn more:** [Transforming code with Amazon Q Developer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/code-transformation.html)

questions.question:
A company is evaluating Amazon Nova models in Amazon Bedrock. The company requires a multimodal model that supports multiple languages.  
  
Which Nova model meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Nova Lite processes text, image, and video inputs, supports the multilingual capabilities of the Nova understanding models, and is AWS’s low-cost multimodal model. Nova Pro is a more capable but higher-cost multimodal option, while Nova Canvas and Nova Reel are specialized image and video generation models.\
\
**Learn more:** [Nova Lite - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-amazon-nova-lite.html) · [Introducing Amazon Nova foundation models](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/introducing-amazon-nova-frontier-intelligence-and-industry-leading-price-performance/)

questions.question:
A company is evaluating Amazon Nova models in Amazon Bedrock. The company requires a multimodal model that supports multiple languages.  
  
Which Nova model meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Deploy optimized small language models (SLMs) on edge devices.
Deploy optimized large language models (LLMs) on edge devices.
Incorporate a centralized small language model (SLM) API for asynchronous communication with edge devices.
Incorporate a centralized large language model (LLM) API for asynchronous communication with edge devices.

questions.explanation:
Deploying optimized small language models on edge devices achieves the lowest latency because inference happens locally without network round trips. SLMs are lightweight and designed to run efficiently within device resource constraints, whereas centralized LLM APIs introduce network latency that contradicts the lowest-latency requirement.

**Learn more:** [Running small language models at the edge](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/running-and-optimizing-small-language-models-on-premises-and-at-the-edge/) · [Machine learning on edge devices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/machine-learning-lens/machine-learning-on-edge-and-on-multiple-platforms.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to build an AI assistant that responds to user queries. The AI assistant must assess particular data sources, call external APIs, generate response choices, and compare and prioritize those choices.  
  
Which Amazon Bedrock feature or resource meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Agents orchestrate interactions among foundation models, data sources, software applications, and user conversations. They can query knowledge bases and invoke external APIs through action groups as part of a multi-step orchestration process, enabling the assistant to generate and prioritize an appropriate response.

**Learn more:** [Automate tasks in your application using AI agents - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html) · [How Amazon Bedrock Agents works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-how.html)

questions.question: Which metric is used to assess the performance of foundation models (FMs) for text-summarization tasks?
questions.explanation:
BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) score measures text generation quality by computing n-gram overlap precision between machine-generated summaries and human reference summaries, with a brevity penalty for overly short outputs. BLEU is widely used for evaluating text generation tasks including summarization. F1 score (A) is for classification, accuracy (C) lacks the granularity needed for generation tasks, and MSE (D) is for regression—none are appropriate for summarization evaluation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Text summarization for model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-tasks-text-summary.html)

questions.question:
A company developed an AI-powered resume-screening system. The company used a large dataset to train the model. The dataset included resumes that did not represent all demographics.  
  
Which core dimension of responsible AI is presented by this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Fairness requires AI systems to avoid unjustified bias and disparate outcomes among demographic groups. Training on resumes that underrepresent some demographics can cause the screening model to perform less equitably for those groups.\
\
**Learn more:** [Core dimensions of responsible AI for Amazon Bedrock applications](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/considerations-for-addressing-the-core-dimensions-of-responsible-ai-for-amazon-bedrock-applications/) · [AWS Well-Architected Responsible AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/responsible-ai-lens/responsible-ai-lens.html)

questions.question:
A company is using domain-specific models. The company wants to avoid creating new models from the beginning. The company instead wants to adapt pre-trained models to create models for new, related tasks.  

Which ML strategy meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Transfer learning leverages pre-trained models that already possess general knowledge, then fine-tunes them on domain-specific data for new but related tasks. This approach avoids building from scratch, saving time and computational resources. Adjusting training epochs, using unsupervised learning, and other options do not address the core requirement of adapting existing models.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Transfer Learning?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/transfer-learning/)

questions.question: Which result follows from increasing a model’s transparency?

options.text: Reduced need for model validation steps
Elimination of regulatory compliance monitoring requirements
Automatic removal of all bias from model predictions
Enhanced ability to identify bias and improve model governance

questions.explanation:
Greater model transparency enables stakeholders to inspect model behavior more effectively, identify potential bias, and improve governance and oversight practices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Model transparency (AWS whitepaper)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/model-explainability-aws-ai-ml/model-transparency.html) · [Responsible AI (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/ai/responsible-ai/)

questions.question:
A company is building a customer service chatbot. The company wants the chatbot to improve its responses by learning from past interactions and online resources.  

Which AI learning strategy provides this self-improvement capability?

options.text: Supervised learning with a manually curated dataset of good responses and bad responses
Reinforcement learning with rewards for positive customer feedback
Unsupervised learning to find clusters of similar customer inquiries
Supervised learning with a continuously updated FAQ database

questions.explanation:
Reinforcement learning with rewards enables continuous self-improvement: the chatbot learns by receiving positive feedback for helpful responses and adjusting its behavior accordingly. This allows autonomous improvement from past interactions without manual dataset updates.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is RLHF? (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedback/)

questions.question:
A hospital is developing an AI system to help doctors diagnose diseases using patient records and medical images. To comply with regulations, sensitive patient data must remain in the country where the data is located.  
  
Which data-governance strategy will ensure compliance and protect patient privacy?
questions.explanation:
Data residency requires data to be stored and handled within a specified geographic jurisdiction. Keeping sensitive patient records and medical images in their country of origin supports location-based regulatory requirements and helps protect patient privacy.\
\
**Learn more:** [Addressing data residency with AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/addressing-data-residency-with-aws/)

options.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the custom model.
Deploy the custom model in an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time inference.
Register the model with the Amazon SageMaker Model Registry.
Grant access to the custom model in Amazon Bedrock.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Bedrock does not support on-demand inference for customized (fine-tuned or continued pre-trained) models — a company must purchase Provisioned Throughput before it can invoke its custom model at all, so this purchase is the mandatory action required to actually use it. Granting model access in the console applies to base models offered by AWS and third-party providers, not to a private custom model that already belongs to the account, so it is not the blocking step here.

**Learn more:** [Purchase Provisioned Throughput for a custom model](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-use-pt.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is training a foundation model (FM). It wants the FM training data to be managed effectively, securely, and compliantly throughout the data lifecycle. The data must adhere to governance practices.  
  
Which option is an AWS data-governance strategy for managing data across its lifecycle?

options.text: Allow unrestricted access to all data for every employee.
Store data indefinitely without classification or retention policies.
Rely solely on manual reviews for data quality and compliance.
Establish data lifecycle policies, access controls, logging, and monitoring.

questions.explanation:
Data governance across a data lifecycle uses lifecycle and retention policies to govern handling and disposal, access controls to limit data use, and logging and monitoring to provide auditability and detect security or compliance issues. AWS Well-Architected guidance specifically includes retention periods, access, auditing, and continuous monitoring as data-lifecycle considerations.

**Learn more:** [AWS Well-Architected Framework: Define scalable data lifecycle management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2025-02-25/framework/sec_data_classification_lifecycle_management.html) · [AWS Enterprise Data Governance Catalog: Data governance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/enterprise-data-governance-catalog/data-governance.html)

questions.question: Which strategy can evaluate the performance of a foundation model (FM) in real-world applications?

options.text: Conducting A/B testing with users in a controlled environment
Human evaluation by subject matter experts
Measuring the model’s accuracy on a training dataset
Analysis of the model’s internal representations and attention patterns

questions.explanation:
Human evaluation by subject-matter experts assesses whether model outputs are accurate, relevant, useful, and appropriate for the domain and intended application. Amazon Bedrock supports human-based evaluations using employees or industry subject-matter experts to rate model responses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Evaluate the performance of Amazon Bedrock resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/evaluation.html)
